articles.title: Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton is out indefinitely after dislocating ankle in win over Raiders
articles.summary: Whether Thornton sustained the injury while being tackle or as he stood up to celebrate the catch, his left foot wasn't pointed in a natural direction.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury late in the fourth quarter of Week 4's 30-27 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"It doesn't look good," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters postgame.

With the Chiefs trailing 19-17, Thornton caught a 55-yard pass from Patrick Mahomes on a post pattern, continuing what had been the most productive game of his career. Thornton was tackled by Raiders safety Treydan Stukes and immediately stood up to celebrate the big play. However, he then crumpled to the turf with his left foot turned in an unnatural direction as he sat on the ground.

Warning: Video of the injury is graphic.

Thornton flew home with the team and will be further evaluated in Kansas City, Reid said.

NFL Network reported Thornton dislocated his ankle, which was put back in place by doctors. He was reportedly "in good spirits" and will be sidelined indefinitely.

Thornton suffered the injury while being tackled, though it wasn't clear in live-action when he stood up. Perhaps adrenaline compelled him to celebrate the big play and reality quickly set in as his left foot touched the grass, but replay showed the ankle being dislocated durign the tackle.

Unable to put weight on his left leg, Thornton was carted off the field and taken to the locker room.

As could be expected, Thornton's teammates were upset after seeing how badly he was hurt and watching him require assistance to leave the game. When play resumed, Kenneth Walker scored on a 2-yard run to give Kansas City a 23-19 lead. A subsequent 2-point conversion attempt failed when Mahomes threw incomplete to Walker.

On the ensuing kickoff, Chiefs linebacker Jeffrey Bassa forced Raiders returner Dareke Young to fumble and the ball was recovered by Jack Cochrane at the Las Vegas 22-yard line. One play later, Walker rushed for his second touchdown in 19 seconds. Harrison Butker followed with the extra point for a 30-19 lead.

Thornton, 26, was developing into a reliable big-play threat for Mahomes and a Chiefs receiver corps thinned out by injuries. Rashee Rice left the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury . Xavier Worthy has also been dealing with a shoulder injury, though he played Sunday, notching four receptions.

Because of the injuries, the Chiefs could explore a potential reunion with free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill, The Athletic's Michael Silver reported Sunday night.

Prior to his injury, Thornton caught five passes for 111 yards and two TDs, including an 8-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter.

"Just praying for him, You never want anyone to get injured and you're hoping it's better than it looked out there," Mahomes said to CBS' Tracy Wolfson after the game. "Praying for him and hopefully he comes back healthy."

Thornton missed final 3 games last season with concussion

This is the second consecutive season in which Thornton had to leave a game due to injury.

Last year in a Week 15 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers, he suffered a concussion on a head-to-head hit by safety Tony Jefferson. Thornton missed the Chiefs' final three games as a result.

The former couple’s split once drew intense attention, but the supermodel is now looking back on their marriage with less pain and more gratitude. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35M Ohio mansion has a $1.75M architectural twin in Illinois
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s new Ohio mansion has an unusual connection to another historic home nearly 400 miles away.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s new Ohio mansion has an unusual connection to another historic home nearly 400 miles away. The Kansas City Chiefs star paid $5.35 million for Moyenage, a grand estate overlooking Lake Erie, but its history stretches beyond football and celebrity real estate. The mansion was designed for the same steel magnate who commissioned a strikingly similar house in Illinois several years earlier. Now, that architectural relative, the House of Seven Gables in Wheaton, is on the market for $1.75 million, offering buyers a rare chance to own a piece of the story behind Kelce’s impressive new property.Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion has a historic architectural connectionKelce’s Bratenahl estate, known as Moyenage, stands out for its scale. The roughly 21,000-square-foot property sits on 3.5 acres overlooking Lake Erie and includes eight bedrooms, a game room, home theatre and a separate two-bedroom gatehouse.But the story behind the house makes the property even more intriguing.Architect Jarvis Hunt originally designed Moyenage for Chicago steel magnate Jay C. Morse around the start of the 20th century. Before that, Hunt had designed the House of Seven Gables in Wheaton, Illinois, for Morse in 1897.Jenny Ames of Engel & Völkers Chicago, who is representing the Illinois property with Lisa Grimes, said the connection is more than a coincidence.“The resemblance is really quite remarkable,”“Historical accounts indicate that when Morse later built Moyenage in Ohio, he asked Hunt to design it based on his Wheaton home,” Ames said. “So when you look at the two houses side by side, you are not simply seeing two homes by the same architect. You are seeing two versions of a very personal architectural vision created for the same owner.”Both properties showcase Tudor and Jacobean influences, with brick exteriors, steep gables, large chimneys and elaborate interiors.House of Seven Gables offers a smaller version of Kelce’s mansionThe Illinois home is considerably smaller than Kelce’s Ohio residence, covering about 10,000 square feet on less than half an acre. It has seven bedrooms, three floors and a newly built three-car garage.Inside, however, its historic character remains strong. Original fireplaces, oak panelling, carved woodwork, flooring, leaded glass and beamed ceilings have survived decades of changes.“The interiors are where the relationship becomes especially interesting,” Ames said. “Both homes have extraordinary woodwork, beamed ceilings, substantial staircases, leaded glass and formal rooms organized on a grand scale.”The property also has an unusual survival story. After serving as the Loretto Convent for decades, the mansion faced demolition during redevelopment. In 2017, workers moved the approximately 730-ton structure about 500 feet to a new site.“They moved the structure intact,” Ames said.The remarkable operation involved placing the mansion on steel beams and 21 hydraulic dollies before moving it onto a new foundation. The process reportedly took about six hours.For Kelce, Moyenage is now part of his growing real estate portfolio. For prospective buyers in Illinois, the House of Seven Gables offers something even more unusual: a chance to own the architectural predecessor of the Chiefs star’s historic Ohio retreat.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ESPN Insider Names Green Bay Packers Starter As Potential Trade Candidate to Watch
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have fallen well short of expectations to this point in the 2026 NFL season, prompting calls […]
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have fallen well short of expectations to this point in the 2026 NFL season, prompting calls from the fan base for a coaching change. While firing Matt LaFleur is unlikely, it does appear there's a chance of Green Bay operating as a mini-seller come trade season.

In an early preview of the 2026 NFL trade deadline, ESPN 's Dan Graziano mentioned Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon as a potential veteran who could be traded within the next month.

"The Packers, like the Chargers, did not expect to have a losing record at this point (or probably any point) of the season. They're dealing with massive injury issues, particularly on the offensive line — the type of thing that can make it very tough to right the ship after a difficult start. Nixon is 29 and in the final year of his contract. He has experience as a kick returner as well as cornerback, and an acquiring team would be on the hook for only a prorated portion of his $4.3 million 2026 salary." ESPN's Dan Graziano on why the Green Bay Packers may trade Keisean Nixon

"The Packers, like the Chargers, did not expect to have a losing record at this point (or probably any point) of the season. They're dealing with massive injury issues, particularly on the offensive line — the type of thing that can make it very tough to right the ship after a difficult start. Nixon is 29 and in the final year of his contract. He has experience as a kick returner as well as cornerback, and an acquiring team would be on the hook for only a prorated portion of his $4.3 million 2026 salary."

ESPN's Dan Graziano on why the Green Bay Packers may trade Keisean Nixon

Nixon, age 29, has served as Green Bay's No. 1 cornerback since last season and he's been a multi-year starter for the last four years. After earning first-team All-Pro honors as a returner (2022-23), he transitioned away from special teams in 2025 to focus exclusively on playing the perimeter and lining up against top receivers.

He earned his first Pro Bowl selection this past season, though that was largely a result of the number of players who declined to participate or were ruled out due to injury. While he got off to a strong start, he wound up allowing a 105.1 passer rating, 651 receiving yards and 6 touchdowns on 87 targets in coverage.

In a contract year, there has been no reporting since the summer that indicated Green Bay wanted to sign Nixon to a long-term extension. He also received some pushback from the Packers coaching staff during training camp and implied the team was punishing him .

Trading away a veteran starting cornerback has been done before by Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst. In October 2023 , Green Bay traded Rasul Douglas and a 2024 fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills in exchange for a third-round pick. The team finished with a 9-8 record, losing in the Divisional Round.

Keisean Nixon contract ( Spotrac ): $7.166 million cap hit in 2026

While Nixon isn't beloved by the fans in Green Bay because he hasn't performed like a No. 1 cornerback, he can be an effective No. 2 starter on a better defense. It also helps that he carries a relatively small cap hit relative to his role, which could make him more appealing now that Joey Porter Jr. is off the market.

Green Bay does have an experienced starter working behind Nixon and rookie Brandon Cisse as a backup right now in Carrington Valentine. However, the team is dangerously thin at the position beyond the trio. If Nixon is being traded within the next month, either the team is riding a five-game losing streak and sits at 2-7 or Cisse has emerged as a true No. 1 option and the team is comfortable putting Valentine back out there full-time. Right now, neither seems likely.

Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that he plans to begin negotiating a deal for the eight-time Pro Bowler with multiple teams on Monday. Schefter noted that one of those teams is the Kansas City Chiefs, who are "very interested" in a reunion with Hill, according to The Athletic's Michael Silver .

Despite the varied interest, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday it would be a "surprise" if Hill signs anywhere besides the Chiefs:

"In the wake of those injuries, the Chiefs have already reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, to express their interest," Silver reported. "They'd have to be satisfied with the receiver's recovery, but there would likely be no other obstacles on the organization's end. It seems like the Chiefs are the frontrunners to land Hill, but other teams will surely try to pry him away before he makes his decision later this week.

articles.title: Any given Sunday: The NFL's parity is its greatest asset
articles.summary: Game-to-game parity is the NFL's crown jewel, what makes the sport so compelling, week after week.
articles.body:
If you happened to be within sight of more than one screen on Sunday around 3:50 p.m. Eastern, either at a sports bar, or with multiview enabled, or with an array of installed man-cave TVs, you would have seen something wonderful unfolding. At almost the exact same moment, you saw multiple late-fourth-quarter scenarios unfolding:

New England, down 26-21, driving against Buffalo;

Los Angeles, down 20-10 against Philadelphia, attempting a miraculous two-possession comeback;

Tampa Bay, down 17-14 to Green Bay, attempting a comeback with a rookie quarterback;

Houston, down 27-23 to Dallas, driving for the go-ahead score … and then Dallas , down 30-27, attempting a scoreboard flip.

Four games, five late defeat-to-victory drives — and four of them were successful. (Sorry, Tampa Bay. And sorry the defense didn't hold, Houston.) Parity reigns supreme in the NFL, as always. Hail to the Shield, and order another round!

"Parity," in this context, doesn't mean there are no dynasties in the NFL, of course. You probably know the famous (and accurate) statistic about how half the NFL's playoff field turns over every year. (The 2025 teams already on pace to miss the 2026 postseason: Green Bay, Pittsburgh, Houston and the Chargers.) But even that's looking from too high a perspective. Drill down to the per-game level, and you'll see the real parity that exists across the league on a weekly basis.

The NFL's perpetual enforcement of parity is no secret, statistically, financially or spiritually. First, some numbers: per a study by NFL Analytics , of the 7,276 games played between 1999 and 2025, 50.7 percent finished with a margin of eight points or fewer between winner and loser. (Another 26.9 percent finished as "blowouts," defined as a margin of 17 points or more.) The percentage of one-possession games is increasing, from 47.9 percent in the 2005-2010 era to 52.7 percent from 2017 to 2025.

Already this year, Week 3 featured 12 of 16 games ending within one possession, tying the most in any single week since 1999. And depending on the outcome of Monday night's Falcons-Saints game, this week, already with 11 of 15 games within a single possession, could match that total.

Statistically, the most common finishing margin of an NFL game isn't just one possession, it's one field goal . According to Pro Football Reference , the top four most common scores in NFL games across history are three-point wins. (Trivia winner for you someday: the most common score in an NFL game is 20-17, achieved 303 times, most recently in Week 2 by Green Bay over the Jets.)

What the NFL has mastered isn't season-long parity. Last season, for instance, featured three 14-3 teams and four 3-14 teams, not exactly a clustering around the median. No, the NFL now specializes in in-game parity — the idea that no matter how far apart two teams may be talent-wise, there's a very good chance the final margin of victory will be within a single possession.

Sunday was a perfect example. Coming into the day, the Bills seemed like the best team in the league by a wide margin, whereas there were real concerns about whether New England's Drake Maye remembered which side of a football to point downfield. Through three weeks, Minnesota seemed like it had leveled up, while Miami looked so bad it might manage to lose 19 games in a 17-game season. And what happened? New England upset Buffalo, while Miami finished an uncomfortably close five points short of Minnesota.

The lesson for teams is obvious: first, no matter the opponent, you can win — or lose — on any given Sunday, so every game matters. Second, the margin between victory and defeat is a tiny one, so the winning teams will be the ones that find those edges, over and over again.

Last year, the Denver Broncos were 11-2 in one-score games, a run that coincided nicely with division rival Kansas City's record of 1-9 in such games. It's better to be lucky than good, but it's even better to be opportunistic than lucky.

This year's version of Denver might be Minnesota, which is 4-0 but won three of those by a single possession. And the hard-luck team of the year — of the last two years, really — is Tampa Bay, which has played 10 straight one-score games and lost eight of them, including all four this season .

The NFL's hard salary cap has created this situation by dispersing talent across the league. Its genius scheduling model, clustering most games within a few time slots, contributes to the energy; there's nothing like those frenetic final minutes of games — what NFL RedZone's Scott Hanson calls "the witching hour" — when teams can vault to victory or collapse in defeat.

And that, for the fan, is what makes parity so thrilling. Your team might win only a third of its games, but it's almost certainly going to be close in a few of those losses. Your team might rack up a division, conference or Super Bowl championship, but it's not going to be a smooth, stress-free ride. Game-to-game parity is the NFL's crown jewel, what makes the sport so compelling, week after week.

So, bottom line: You'd better go set up another screen or two for this weekend. Just in case.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill reportedly planning to sign with new team 'in next few days' with Chiefs among the potential suitors
articles.summary: Hill has been recovering from multiple torn ligaments he suffered in his left knee last season.
articles.body:
Tyreek Hill is beginning to negotiate with teams on his potential return, his agent told ESPN on Monday .

"I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days," Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The Kansas City Chiefs are among those teams and are reportedly working toward a reunion with Hill after losing two receivers to injury during their 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.

Kansas City had already reached out to Rosenhaus, The Athletic's Michael Silver reported on Sunday. Following Sunday's win, several Chiefs players — including quarterback Patrick Mahomes — told Silver that they would be in favor of bringing Hill back once he's healthy enough to play.

During Sunday's game versus the Raiders, the Chiefs lost Rashee Rice to a hamstring injury and Tyquan Thornton with a dislocated left ankle . Xavier Worthy has also been struggling with a shoulder injury, though he did play against Las Vegas.

Hill, 31, is working his way back from a serious knee injury suffered last year in the Miami Dolphins' fourth game of the season. As he made a catch going out of bounds, Hill planted hard on his left leg as Jets defensive back Malachi Moore wrapped up his right leg.

The veteran receiver was left with his lower leg pointing in the wrong direction. Dolphins athletic trainers had to cut his cleat off before stabilizing his leg. Hill was eventually diagnosed with a dislocated kneecap and multiple torn ligaments in his left knee.

The Dolphins released Hill in February , making him a free agent for the first time in his NFL career. However, no team signed him because of his knee injury, putting his football future in doubt.

In late July, as NFL teams were reporting to training camp, Hill posted a video to social media that showed his progress in running barefoot and making jumps out of his swimming pool.

In the video, Hill also revealed that doctors told him that he might not be able to walk again because of the injury, let alone resume his NFL career. Despite running, he also said that he had "no power in my left leg at all," which was the biggest step he had to take in working his way back.

Hill played six seasons for the Chiefs, who drafted him in the fifth round in 2016. He was named to the Pro Bowl in each of those six seasons, also earning first-team All-Pro honors three times. Altogether, Hill compiled 479 receptions for 6,630 yards and 56 touchdowns in 91 games and helped Kansas City win Super Bowl LIV .

Seeking a contract extension, Hill was traded to the Dolphins for five draft picks before the 2022-23 season. He subsequently signed a four-year, $120 million extension. In his four seasons with Miami, Hill had two 119-catch seasons, led the league with 1,799 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns in 2023, and made two more Pro Bowl and first-team All-Pro squads.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Rips 'Dumb' Underdog Label After Giants' Win to Be 1st in NFC East Standings
articles.summary: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo wanted to prove a point in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo wanted to prove a point in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

"It's dumb. It's dumb to be underdogs at home, especially when you're a good football team," he told reporters after the game. "When people want to bet against you at your own place and you have a team coming from a six-hour flight on a time change, it's a pretty brutal feeling as a team when you feel you're put underneath them. We came out here and handled business."

The Giants didn't earn a lot of style points in their victory. Skattebo and Najee Harris combined to run for 88 yards on 27 carries, while quarterback Jameis Winston delivered what's a trademark performance for him. He threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns but had two interceptions and got sacked four times.

New York benefited from Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett throwing three interceptions himself. The last one was a pick-six on the game's final play with Arizona looking at 4th-and-goal from the 4-yard line.

Skattebo has every right to savor the result and call out the Giants' skeptics with his squad leading the NFC East at 3-1.

But the final score is a little deceiving as to how close New York was to validating its underdog status.

articles.title: QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 4
articles.summary: Take a look around the league and some major surprises jump to the forefront. Those situations are mainly due to each team's quarterback play or how they're protecting the position. In Carolina, the Panthers' Bryce Young has grown into the league's top passer. The Cleveland Browns own a 3-1 record because their quarterback position is no longer a black hole pulling the rest of the team into its vortex. The Las Vegas Raiders may have come up short this past weekend, but Kirk Cousins has been everything the team hoped he could be until Fernando Mendoza eventually takes the reins. Conversely, the New York Giants, Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears aren't allowing the quarterback position to be a hindrance toward a successful start.
articles.body:
Take a look around the league and some major surprises jump to the forefront. Those situations are mainly due to each team's quarterback play or how they're protecting the position. In Carolina, the Panthers' Bryce Young has grown into the league's top passer. The Cleveland Browns own a 3-1 record because their quarterback position is no longer a black hole pulling the rest of the team into its vortex. The Las Vegas Raiders may have come up short this past weekend, but Kirk Cousins has been everything the team hoped he could be until Fernando Mendoza eventually takes the reins. Conversely, the New York Giants, Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears aren't allowing the quarterback position to be a hindrance toward a successful start.

Each week, Bleacher Report grades every quarterback performance to provide context for individual play and how it affects their respective squads.

ARI | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Stat Line : 21 of 35 for 166 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions

At 1-3, the idea of the Arizona Cardinals moving on from starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett has become a talking point. Though head coach Mike LaFleur immediately shot down the possibility of a change at this point.

Even so, the questions will continue if Brissett doesn't play well enough and the Cardinals fail.

"[The offense] just kind got in our own way again," Brissett told reporters . "It was tough, because our defense was playing so well. We were trying to capitalize on the stop they were getting. I mean, two turnovers, you can't do that." Eventually, something needs to change. The Cardinals face the Detroit Lions, Los Angeles Rams (twice), Denver Broncos, Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs before Thanksgiving. It's a brutal schedule. Brissett has proved he can only do so much. A look at another quarterback will be necessary sooner rather than later.

Baltimore Ravens: Lamar Jackson & Tyler Huntley

Stat Line : Jackson, 15 of 20 for 222 yards and two touchdowns; Huntley, eight of nine for 63 yards

The Baltimore Ravens did all of the work they needed to do Sunday before Lamar Jackson left the contest with a high-ankle sprain.

Jackson and Co. scored 24 first-half points. By the time Huntley entered the lineup at the start of the third quarter, the Ravens simply needed to hold on and milk the clock.

With Huntley leading the way, Baltimore punted on four of its five drives (not including late-game knee-downs). Fortunately, Jackson is believed to be day-to-day, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

"We obviously played maybe a little more bit more conservative in the second half with the weather and the lead," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters . "Proud of 'Snoop' [Huntley] coming in there when his number's called."

Score : 29-26 loss vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 23 of 33 for 253 yards, a touchdown, an interception and a rushing score

Josh Allen can do anything on a football field, which is both a positive and a negative. Usually, Allen makes the necessary plays to give the Buffalo Bills an advantage. He also take unnecessary risks that can lead to significant mistakes.

Case in point, Allen threw an interception Sunday with under two minutes to go while the Bills trailed by three points. The quarterback initially avoided a free-rusher by spinning out of the pressure then heaved the ball into double-coverage, which safety Craig Woodson snagged.

"Essentially, I mean, live bullets," Allen said when he asked if he threw that specific pass blindly. "It's happening quick, make a guy miss and you feel like you have a one-on-one ball, and the safety made a good play."

More times than not, the former NFL MVP delivers. There's a certain confidence in what's capable of doing. Some might argue its overconfidence, because he's also prone to attempt throws that he shouldn't.

New NFL contenders starting to emerge after Week 4

Stat Line : 29 of 41 for 319 yards and two touchdowns

Bryce Young leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards through four weeks of play, and the Carolina Panthers feature the league's top-ranked aerial attack.

Think about those facts for a few seconds. Let them marinate. Now, understand Young is two years removed from being benched by head coach Dave Canales despite being the No. 1 overall pick from the 2023 class. He only got the job back in 2024 because Andy Dalton suffered an injury from a car wreck.

Now, Young is cooking and looks every bit the part of a franchise quarterback. He shredded the Detroit Lions' porous secondary during Sunday Night Football despite wide receivers Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette being on injured reserve.

"Nothing that Bryce did shocked me today," Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters . "Bryce is a hell of a quarterback, man. He just is. He's dangerous, he's got a quick release. He can process it, he can see it, he's mobile, he can move around in the pocket. He was tough, tough today."

Stat Line : 25 of 34 for 268 yards and an interception

Despite an outstanding outside by veteran Case Keenum during Monday Night Football six days earlier, the Chicago Bears turned to Tyson Bagent to start against the New York Jets.

"Tyson has earned the right to be our No. 2 quarterback," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters . "I have a lot of confidence in him. I thought he played really well today, efficient with the football. ... I thought he had a great job with the operation."

Keenum only started during the previous contest, because Bagent was cleared from the NFL's concussion protocol early enough to prepare properly for that contest. He resumed his role as the team's QB2—which is the Bears' de facto starter while Caleb Williams deals with a hamstring injury. Bagent was efficient for most of the contest, but he benefited greatly from a ground-and-pound attack that generated 232 rushing yards and allowed the Bears told hold the ball for nearly 43 minutes.

Score : 22-17 loss vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 39 of 54 for 428 yards, a touchdown, two interceptions and a rushing score

Once again, the Cincinnati Bengals are asking to much of their quarterback, Joe Burrow.

The team got off to a 2-0 start, because it was playing complementary football. During Sunday's contest, Burrow threw the ball 54 times. He did so, because the Jacksonville Jaguars shut down the run game. Furthermore, Burrow had to drop back a season-high 54 times—the third-most in his career—without the help of star wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, both of whom left Sunday's contest due to injuries.

Burrow is capable of handling that much responsibility and continue dealing. He wants the ball in his hands even if the offense becomes one-dimensional and he's forced into a couple of turnovers.

"My response to that would be, 'Let me throw it more,'" Burrow told reporters . "Because I know we are great at it. Because I know that's what I do best and we're really pass-protecting well right now. Obviously, we'd like to get more out of the run game, but you know I know we'll make it work."

Score : 27-24 win vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Stat Line : 24 of 33 for 268 yards, a touchdown, an interception and a fumble lost

In what many would deem as an unbelievable turn of events, the Cleveland Browns are 3-1 and Deshaun Watson is playing well enough to quiet any conversation about Shedeur Sanders getting in the lineup.

"While team sources indicated that Watson's performance through three games hasn't convinced the Browns to consider Watson the long-term answer, Cleveland's surprising start has shifted the conversation inside the building to whether the 31-year-old passer and the Browns can build short-term momentum," ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi reported last week.

Then, the Browns won another game. This time, they did so against the rival Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson had stretches of excellent play. Though he missed some throws, particularly late in the contest.

Cleveland still has plenty to figure out in the coming months, but a winning record and the quarterback position not holding the entire team back definitely change the conversation.

Stat Line : 32 of 45 for 335 yards and a touchdown

Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb share a special connection. The two have never been better working together than they were Sunday against the Houston Texans.

Lamb caught 17 passes for 189 yards and the game-winning touchdown. In doing so, he became the first player in Cowboys history with at least 15 receptions, 150 yards and a touchdown grab, according to NFL Researcher . But he doesn't reach any of those achievements without Prescott continually delivering the ball accurately and on time.

During the game-winning drive, Prescott completed eight of 11 passes, including the 22-yard scoring strike to Lamb on a skinny post.

"That's just credit to who he is, the way he's shown up each and every day, been a professional and just grown," Prescott told reporters . "And the communication, just the open communication we're able to have. I think that's the difference in where we are right now than where we have been in the past."

Score : 24-14 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers

Stat Line : 25 of 42 for 214 yards and a touchdown

The Denver Broncos continue to sleep through the first half of games. The team managed a lone field goal Sunday before the break. Something needs to change, because Denver has scored only 13 first-half points through four games.

"We've got to figure it out fast," head coach Sean Payton told reporters . "We're going into Week 5."

Due to the circumstances, Davis Webb's standing as offensive-play-caller has come under fire.

"I think when you look at the overall landscape, we've played four of the tops teams in the league. [It's] not easy for a first-time OC as young as he is to go against some of the, quite frankly, best teams in the league," Bo Nix t old reporters . " ... I think it's just overall something that we have to continue to help him and execute. As players, we have to put him in a better spot."

Nix isn't helping the situation, though. He's not pushing the ball down the field to stretch opposing defenses. The third-year quarterback completed one pass over 12 yards Sunday and none at a depth of 20 or more.

Score : 32-26 loss vs. Carolina Panthers

Stat Line : 32 of 52 for 412 yards and a touchdown

What more can the Detroit Lions ask of their quarterback? Jared Goff threw for over 400 yards Sunday and didn't commit any turnovers. He tried to carry his team to victory, but Detroit's defense wouldn't let him.

After the Carolina Panthers punted on their first offensive possession, Bryce Young and Co. scored points during their next six drives. Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan torched Detroit's underwhelming secondary for a career-high 14 receptions and 192 yards.

The Lions are currently ranked dead last in total defense. Conversely, Goff has orchestrated a top-three passing offense. Detroit is top six in total offense. The quarterback has yet to produce a turnover through four games. Somehow, it's not enough, which has to be frustrating.

"But yeah, whole season ahead of us and a whole lot of ball ahead of us and a lot of things to get right," Goff told reporters . "And I know one thing: We're going to stick together and stay insulated in our bubble and lean on each other and make it right."

Score : 17-14 win vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : 22 of 30 for 197 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Last week, Jordan Love said the following , "That's an area that we've got to improve on, is in pass pro, just making sure we're going to the right people and sustaining blocks for as long as we can, giving me some time to be able to pick the defense apart."

During Sunday's contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Love wasn't sacked and hit only twice. The quarterback responded with his highest completion percentage (73.3) and quarterback rating (98.9) so far this season.

"[The offensive line] did a great job," Love told reporters , "and you could feel the difference back there, for sure." Love's numbers could have been even better if not for a few key drops. But the quarterback and his team will be happen getting the win going into this weekend's rivalry contest with the Chicago Bears.

Stat Line : 21 of 31 for 347 yards and two touchdowns

CJ Stroud made his 50th start for the Houston Texans Sunday and he's no longer viewed as the problem. Instead, the Texans defense is the unit that's currently struggling.

Stroud led a nine-play, 87-yard drive to take a lead with just over two minutes remaining. Houston's defense failed to stop CeeDee Lamb and the Dallas Cowboys' offense during the ensuing drive. From there, the Texans didn't have enough time to answer.

The quarterback still took the blame after the game, even though his unit generated nearly 400 yards of offense and averaged 7.6 yards per play.

At 0-4, Houston's season is essentially over. Only one team in NFL history has come back from such a poor start and still made the postseason. Though Stroud can continue to build on what he's done so far and ensure he's Houston's long-term answer at the game's most important position.

Score : 30-13 win vs. Washington Commanders

Stat Line : 19 of 34 for 143 yards, an interception, a fumble lost and a rushing score

The Indianapolis Colts are winning in spite of Daniel Jones. The team's QB1 has turned the ball over five times during the last two contests. The Colts won both games despite a turnover deficiency.

"They're all different," Jones told reporters when asked about his turnovers. "I think you gotta understand when to take a chance, when not to, when to protect the ball … I definitely gotta do a better job taking care of the ball."

Jones has suffered from a near-disastrous combination of poor decision-making and unacceptable ball-handling. He has seven turnovers through four weeks of play. A season ago, Jones didn't commit his seventh turnover until Week 9. Fortunately, his feet allowed him to score a touchdown Sunday in London, while also leaning heavily on the Colts' ground game.

Score : 22-17 win vs. Cincinnati Bengals

Stat Line : 18 of 23 for 227 yards and a touchdown

The Jacksonville Jaguars went from being one of the league's most efficient squads to playing their sloppiest game of the season. Trevor Lawrence and Co. still overcame the Cincinnati Bengals.

Officials called the Jaguars for 13 penalties. Jacksonville converted less than 50 percent of its third-down attempts. Also, Lawrence was a sacked a season-high four times.

Lawrence provided a steadying presence. Jacksonville's quarterback was particularly good working the middle of the field, where he completed 11 of 13 passes for 151 yards and his only touchdown, per Sumer Sports' Shawn Syed . He's been this way all season.

As The Athletic's Mike Sando noted , "Lawrence has posted career bests through four games—by a wide margin—in completion rate (69.2 percent), yards per attempt (8.1), passer rating (111.2) and EPA per pass play (0.20). Lawrence also has zero fumbles."

Patrick Mahomes certainly didn't provide an proficient outing against the Las Vegas Raiders. He did provide a winning effort, though. Mahomes completed only 50 percent of his passes. The number tied his lowest completion percentage ever in a Chiefs victory. In the end the Chiefs' desperately needed a play and Mahomes delivered. On 3rd-and-5 and trailing by two points with less than four minutes to play, he connected with Tyquan Thornton for a 55-yard pass, which led to the game-winning touchdown a play later. Mahomes' ability to stare down the blitz and still make a fantastic throw was the difference in this particular game. It's something he's done time and time again, which is why the Chiefs have been so successful for such a long period. Now, they're 4-0 for the fifth time since Mahomes became the team's starting quarterback.

Score : 30-27 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs

Stat Line : 31 of 52 for 365 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

No one actually expected the Las Vegas Raiders to remain perfect, did they? A 3-1 record is still an excellent start and surpasses preseason expectations for this squad.

Kirk Cousins has been a bright spot despite being a bridge quarterback. He's showed he still has plenty left in the tank and going punch-for-punch with Patrick Mahomes only proves that point.

Unfortunately, Cousins' worst play came when his team needed him the most. During the Raiders' final offensive possession trailing by three points with over a minute left to play, the Raiders quarterback completed four of 11 passes and threw an interception after trying to escape pressure—which is not a strength within his game.

To be fair, the Raiders could have been in a much better position to win had the coaching staff not been as aggressive with its decisions earlier in the contest. But the team played to win and it backfired.

"You play through the smoke," Cousins told reporters . "You give yourself a chance at the end of the game. That's what happened today, and we just weren't able to capitalize."

Stat Line : 19 of 31 for 189 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble lost; six carries for 40 yards

Justin Herbert went from playing at an elite level in 2025 to being one of the NFL's worst quarterbacks less than a year later.

The same tools are still present. The Los Angeles Chargers were supposed to have a better supporting cast around him this season. Yet Herbert has been particularly terrible when trying to drive the ball down the field. According to NFL Researcher , the Chargers QB has the league's lowest passer rating when attempting downfield passes combined with the most interceptions. He also has the league's worst QBR among quarterbacks with four starts.

The Seattle Seahawks did heat Herbert up Sunday, with four sacks and 10 quarterback hits. Seattle pressured the quarterback on 46 percent of his dropbacks, per ESPN's Brady Henderson . Something has to give. Herbert isn't anywhere near this bad. The Chargers certainly have enough talent where the team shouldn't be winless through four weeks of play. Right now, they are.

Score : 24-20 win vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Stat Line : 32 of 51 for 317 yards and two interceptions

Matthew Stafford has suffered significant regression after last season's MVP performance. His turnover rate through the first four weeks of play is alarming.

The 38-yard-old veteran already threw six interceptions, including two Sunday, through four weeks of play. He has nine all of last season, which counts postseason contests.

During Stafford's latest outing, he airmailed two passes that led to turnovers. To his credit, he performed at a high level during the second half when the Los Angeles Rams required a 10-point fourth-quarter comeback to secure the victory. The Rams quarterback completed 12 of 15 passes through the team's final two offensive possessions (not including a kneel-down).

"We didn't play our best today," Stafford told reporters , "but we found a way to win the football game. That's what it's all about. We'd love to come out and score every time we touch the ball. That's just not the case in the NFL. ... It wasn't all pretty in the fourth quarter, either. We had opportunities we let slip through in all three phases."

Score : 15-10 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings

Stat Line : nine of 17 for 85 yards and a fumble lost; two carries for 11 yards

The Minnesota Vikings defense is a test for any NFL quarterback. The Miami Dolphins' Malik Willis failed the test. Each week the same statement can be made about how the Dolphins don't have enough surrounding talent for Willis to succeed. While true, the quarterback also needs to hold up his end of the bargain. Willis has the capabilities as an outstanding athlete to make some plays along the way. To be fair, Willis created one big play after avoiding pressure, rolling to his right and finding wide receiver Chris Bell along the sideline. The play should have been a 68-yard touchdown. Instead, the rookie accidentally stepped out of bounds prior to the pass which led to an illegal touching penalty. Otherwise, the Dolphins mustered little offense. The unit finished with under 200 yards. Running back Ollie Gordon II generated 100 by himself. Meanwhile, the passing game was basically non-existent.

Kyler Murray's counterpart Sunday, Malik Willis, has built-in excuses why the Miami Dolphins performed so poorly. Murray doesn't. Justin Jefferson may not have been in the lineup due to an injury, but the Minnesota Vikings still had running back Aaron Jones Sr., wide receiver Jordan Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson on the field. The left side of Minnesota's offensive line sustained injuries, which became problematic. Even so, the Vikings still featured a superior roster. Yet Murray and Co. failed to finish drives. Will Reichard was Minnesota's most effective performer by converting all five of his field-goal attempts. The Vikings' offense didn't score during its three red-zone trips. The unit finished eight of 18 during third-down attempts. More should be expected from Murray. Maybe everyone saw a glimpse of what Murray can become after a strong fourth-quarter effort, where he completed 13 of 14 passes. It's a potential stepping stone for offensive improvement as a whole.

Stat Line : 22 of 37 for 269 yards, three touchdowns, an interception and a fumble lost; eight carries for 54 yards

Drake Maye continues to make mistakes. But he finally delivered Sunday against the Buffalo Bills.

This season has been rough on the second-year signal-caller. Maye has been far too generous when it comes to turnovers. He still gave the ball away twice during his latest outing. The New England Patriots quarterback also threw the game-winning touchdown with under two minutes to play and knocked off a previously undefeated rival. Maye even led his team with 54 rushing yards.

"I got full trust in myself, and I think (the way) my teammates came and pumped me up this week was cool," Maye told reporters . "That's what made this game so special."

Plenty of room for improvement still exists, but the Sunday's performance allows Maye to regather and move past his poor start to campaign.

Stat Line : 18 of 29 for 250 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions

Jameis Winston isn't like other backup quarterbacks. He's a former No. 1 overall pick, with extensive starting experience. His performances can be a wild ride, but he has the ability to make all of the throws and move an offense.

He's also the type of quarterback, who loves to live on the edge and attempt throws that will hurt his team as often as they help.

The full "Jameis Winston experience" occurred Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. In the end, the Giants found a way to win and improve to 3-1. Meanwhile, Winston's confidence is building.

"I'm heating up. And I'm starting to get better, better and better," Winston told reporters . "Last week, I was questioning if I can even throw. This week, I got people talking about the Jameis Winston experience again"

Stat Line : eight of 15 for 119 yards and a touchdown

Geno Smith had been a pleasant surprise to start this season. However, the Chicago Bears didn't allow Smith or the New York Jets offense to do much of anything Sunday.

In fact, the Bears manufacture more first downs than the Jets had offensive plays. New York managed one offensive possession with more than six plays. The Jets' only touchdown came trailing by 17 points in the fourth quarter when Smith connected with Isaiah Williams on a 58-yard score.

Ultimately, Smith didn't do nearly enough Sunday. As a result, his team now owns a 1-3 record.

"You've got to get back to work and you've got to demand it from yourself," Smith said after the game . "It starts with the man in the mirror."

Stat Line : 12 of 27 for 93 yards and two touchdowns

The more things change; the more they stay the same.

A season ago, the Philadelphia Eagles experienced long stretch of stagnant offensive play. The growing divide between quarterback Jalen Hurts and top wide receiver AJ Brown was believed to be the primary issue. Brown was traded this offseason. However, the Eagles offense continues to have the same problems.

"It's about finding a flow as an offense," Hurts told reporters after Sunday's loss. " … We have not done that."

Hurts added , "I've got to figure it out. However it looks, whatever it means. Find a way to win the game."

An 0-12 effort on third down became the worst outing in Eagles franchise history. Of course, all of the unit's issues don't fall on the quarterback. But everyone has seen too many poor stretches of play from Hurts and Co. not to at least place some of the blame on the quarterback.

Stat Line : 22 of 40 for 399 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions

The Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves at a crossroads.

Aaron Rodgers is trying to ride off into the sunset of a championship season. He can still get the job done, but he's an aging gunslinger who's not as quick or deadly as he once was. At the same time, his posse isn't helping matters. The Steelers' wide receiver struggle mightily to create separation and provide Rodgers with available targets.

As a result, the Steelers are failing to build any consistency within their offense.

"I wouldn't say it was our cleanest game all the way around," Rodgers said after Thursday's loss to the Cleveland Browns. "They were getting after us on some of the long yardage stuff that we weren't winning a bunch. I missed some throws I usually hit."

Stat Line : 19 of 30 for 218 yards and two touchdowns; 10 carries for 29 yards

Brock Purdy wasn't as efficient as he had been through the first three weeks of play, but he gave the Denver Broncos a taste of their own medicine by picking them apart during the second half.

San Francisco took control of the game by scoring touchdowns during its final three offensive possessions (not including kneel-downs). Purdy completed 10 of 11 passes along the way.

The Niners quarterback does benefit from the league's best pass protection. In fact, he's yet to be sacked through four games. But he's also executing at a high level. Purdy took advantage of the Broncos being down their starting cornerbacks, which is exactly what he should do.

"We finished drives and capitalized on opportunities," Purdy said during a postgame game interview with Matt Lively of CBS Sports Bay Area . "... At the end when we needed it, we had to step up and do our thing."

Score : 30-23 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 13 of 22 for 168 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Sam Darnold hasn't looked comfortable leading the Seattle Seahawks offense since coming back from an injury in Week 3.

Darnold threw a poor interception during the Seahawks' first offensive play Sunday, which came directly after Justin Herbert threw an interception to give Seattle excellent field position. Darnold's two touchdowns passes came courtesy of a screen pass to running back Emmanuel Wilson and two-yard slant pattern to Tory Horton for a six-yard score. Without those two quick hitters, Darnold threw for 139 yards.

Furthermore, Seattle converted only three of 12 third-down attempts. As a team, the Seahawks endured 150 penalty yards and still won the contest. Everyone in Seattle's locker room understands this type of effort isn't good enough, even if it ended in a victory.

"We're really grateful for where we're at right now and excited to move forward," head coach Mike Macdonald told reporter s. "But we also understand that we have definitely a lot of room for improvement with our operation, how we take care of the football and obviously the penalties are something we need to address."

Score : 17-14 loss vs. Green Bay Packers

Stat Line : 19 of 27 for 148 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions; eight carries for 55 yards

The possibility of a rookie quarterback starting early in the season can be exciting. Usually, that scenario involves a recent high-round draft pick. In the case of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, a dislocated thumb on Baker Mayfield's throwing hand thrust undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels into the lineup. Expectedly, the Buccaneers came up short Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. But Daniels had the ball in his hands with Tampa Bay trailing by three points and under two minutes to play. The first-time starter didn't deliver, but he also didn't wilt under the pressure.

"Obviously, I'm not happy with the result," Daniels told reporters . "At this position, you want to do everything you can to win a football game. We ended up coming up short. ... We'll look at what's on film. Own that, then get ready to play Thursday Night Football ."

Stat Line : 20 of 31 for 222 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Cam Ward is clearly frustrated with his situation. The 2025 first overall draft pick has not played particularly well and he's been questioned at every turn. Despite everything, he has showed some improvement.

As ESPN's Turron Davenport noted , courtesy of NFL Next Gen Stats, "Ward completed 10 of his 13 quick attempts for 65 yards and 10 of his 18 attempts longer than 2.5 seconds for a season-high 157 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Ward faced pressure on 34.3 percent of dropbacks, the second-lowest mark of the season, completing five of nine attempts for a season-high 40 yards, his touchdown and an interception. Without pressure, Ward went 15 of 22 for 182 yards, another season-high mark." Ward has been consistently pressured this season, which has made life difficult. Like any other quarterback, he performs better from a clean pocket. At the same time, these little improvement must turn into tangible results. Otherwise, they won't be enough to save the quarterback if the team continues to lose and he's not making the caliber of plays worthy of his draft status.

Washington Commanders: Athan Kaliakmanis

Score : 30-13 loss vs. Indianapolis Colts

Stat Line : 15 of 33 for 186 yards, one touchdown and an interception

Marcus Mariota got off to a quick start before suffering a knee injury Sunday. Seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis took the reins and gave the Washington Commanders a chance against the Indianapolis Colts.

Specifically, Kaliakmanis wasn't afraid to challenge the Colts' secondary at the third level. He completed two throws of over 40 yards to Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown. The Commanders also had a 87-yard connection between Kaliakmanis and fellow rookie Antonio Williams called back because of an illegal shift. In fact, he attempted six passes of over 30 yards, according to RotoWire's Ian Hartitz .

Obviously, Kaliakmanis didn't get first-team reps throughout the week and wasn't expected to play. So, he attacked where he could even if the game-plan wasn't specifically built for him. As such, the rookie deserves credit for making some plays and not letting the Colts defense completely overwhelm him.

However, Jayden Daniels is expected to play in Week 5 after missing the last two games.

articles.title: No stadium has a story like the Superdome
articles.summary: The Superdome has weathered the highest of highs and the lowest of lows to represent the complicated and celebrated history of its city.
articles.body:
Editor's note: This story was originally published on April 1, 2012. It has been updated.

NEW ORLEANS — The first thing you notice on the drive into New Orleans is the giant bronze spaceship that's landed at the foot of a modest skyline. It's sleek, shiny, windowless, and in a town bursting with old-world character and charm, fits in like a disco ball in a room full of rocking chairs.

At first glance, it's an oddity more than a marvel, which is maybe why, despite all the evidence in its favor, no one's really noticed that over the last 40-plus years the Superdome has become the most historically significant sporting venue in America.

You want seminal moments? The Superdome is where a college freshman named Michael Jordan nailed a jumper to lift North Carolina over Georgetown; it's where Roberto Duran told Sugar Ray Leonard, "No más"; it's where William "The Refrigerator" Perry barreled into the end zone in Super Bowl XX; it's where Chris Webber called a timeout Michigan didn't have; it's where Adam Vinatieri kicked a field goal as time ran out to give Tom Brady his first Super Bowl win. It's where the lights went out in the middle of Super Bowl XLVII.

And, in 1978, it's where Muhammad Ali won his last fight in front of 65,000 fans.

(Quick aside: During the fight, the ring started to make strange noises, so several engineers crawled underneath it and found that some of the support beams were sagging. Unable to stop the fight for repairs, the engineers did the only thing they could: they held up the beams with their hands as the fight went on above.)

Since the Louisiana Superdome (as it was then known) opened its doors in 1975, it's hosted more Super Bowls (eight) than any other venue, more NCAA tournament championships and spawned the spectacle that is the modern-day Final Four.

In the 1970s, oil and gas provided the jobs and paid the bills in New Orleans. Not so anymore. With one industry moving out, another had to fill the void. Last year tourism pumped $10.8 billion into the local economy.

The Superdome is a big part of the attraction. Each year, the Superdome pumps a reported $600 million into the Louisiana economy.

"It's not just the hard dollars, but the image and the brand of New Orleans," Doug Thornton, who ran the Superdome for 29 years before stepping down earlier this year, told Yahoo Sports in 2012. "It's the first thing you see when you drive in from the airport. It dominates the skyline. And there've been so many memorable moments that have played out here."

Monday night, the Saints will host the Falcons, where the city will celebrate the 20th anniversary of the return to the Superdome in the wake of Hurricane Katrina. They will honor Steve Gleason, who provided the highlight in that game that signaled the "Rebirth" of not only the dome but the city.

And to think, the dome owes its survival to the hurricane that tried to blow it down.

As with all things in New Orleans, time is measured pre- and post-Katrina.

Pre-Katrina, the Superdome was a place some residents of New Orleans loved and others tolerated. Though just 25 years old at the turn of the century, it was outdated by modern stadium standards and was the lone dome of its day still being utilized. With the Astrodome, Silverdome and Kingdome all replaced, the Superdome stood as a relic. It didn't help that the Saints hadn't done much to generate a great deal of nostalgia toward the place.

And so in the summer of 2005, before Katrina hit, talks were underway about what to do with the dome. Update it? Tear it down and build something new? Both presented problems. The government wasn't keen on forking over a couple hundred million bucks to renovate an antique, but then tearing down the dome and building a new one would come with a price tag of $1 billion and a timeline of about four years. New Orleans didn't have the money or the time.

The decision-makers were at an impasse. Then Hurricane Katrina forced their hand.

When Katrina reached land at 5:30 a.m. on Aug. 29, 2005, her 140-mph winds ripped off parts of the Superdome roof. Water poured inside, where 25,000-30,000 refugees sought shelter from the storm. Over the next four days, the Superdome went from a place where games were played to a living hell. Thornton, who was in the dome when the hurricane hit and didn't leave until everyone was evacuated four days later, described the scene inside as "chaotic, inhumane, hot, smelly. The worst that you can think of plus 10."

On Sept. 1, the dome was finally cleared out and Thornton retreated to Baton Rouge. Flying west in a helicopter, he asked the pilot to steer toward his home. He didn't know if it was under water. It was.

"I never will forget looking back over my left shoulder and seeing the dome in the distance and the water glistening the entire four miles to the Superdome, smoke billowing in the background and that was the moment that I said, 'It's over.' " Thornton recalled. "I thought, 'What now? Your city's gone. Can it ever get rebuilt?' I cried all the way to Baton Rouge on that helicopter."

Two days later, he sprung into action. He first set about determining whether or not the Superdome was still structurally sound. A team of engineers determined it was.

Tearing it down and starting over wasn't an option because, one, the city and state didn't have the cash and, two, being without a stadium for four years would have been the catalyst for the Saints to take residence in San Antonio.

"One of the things [Thornton] said that rang home," explained Bill Curl, who worked in public relations at the Superdome for 33 years, "was that if the dome is laying there in a state of disrepair, what would that tell the rest of the world about this city? What message would that send out that our biggest investment was just laying there because of that storm, and our teams had left, our events had left. We'd just be going on about whatever we can make happen here – what was left of us."

Convinced they had to save the dome, Thornton took his case to the governor's office and said, "If you want to keep the city afloat, we gotta put this place back together quickly. It's the symbolism and it's the jobs."

Then Gov. Kathleen Blanco said yes, and Thornton went back to work.

The proposed two-year, $350-million project took just nine months to complete. The motivation to rush was twofold. One, getting the dome up and running was a symbolic gesture that would declare the city was back. Two, then-NFL commissioner Paul Tagliabue wanted the Saints' home opener to be in New Orleans, not Baton Rouge or San Antonio.

While seminal, the finest moment the Superdome has ever witnessed isn't Ali's win, Vinatieri's kick or even the Pope's visit in 1987. It came during a pregame concert on Sept. 25, 2006 — the day the dome re-opened. There, on stage before the Saints were to take on the Atlanta Falcons , was U2 and Green Day singing to a frenzied crowd that hadn't had much to celebrate for a while.

The crowds arrived early that day, many catching up with friends they hadn't seen since the storm hit. Even though they hadn't spoken in more than a year, they didn't have to trade stories to know the pain, because Katrina didn't discriminate. She had affected them all.

Going to their seats inside the dome was a sort of homecoming, a signal that normalcy, a snippet of it anyway, had returned to New Orleans. And there was Bono, telling them as much.

"The SAINTS are coming," he sang. "The SAINTS are coming."

"Look, I'm a football guy. Play the national anthem, get the teams out there and let's play the game. I wasn't big on festivities," recalled Curl. "But when they started to sing, 'The Saints are coming,' oh my goodness. You couldn't find a person that wasn't crying.

"I saw 300-pound football players walking out of that tunnel with tears in their eyes," he continued. "Then, when Steve Gleason blocked that punt and the Saints scored that first touchdown, the celebration started and didn't end until well after that game. The Falcons didn't have a prayer in that game, and you know what, I think they knew it."

As he retold the story 15 years ago, more than half a decade after the fact, Curl's eyes filled with tears.

"With the reopening and the emotion after Katrina, this city truly put its arms around the Superdome and said, 'This is our Superdome.' "

The dome is 51 now. Whenever it does go, it will have witnessed more triumph and tragedy than just about any other venue in the world. It will have, quite simply, lived up to its name as a super dome.
