(New York Daily News Archive via Getty Images)

A statue titled Rebirth featuring the likeness of former New Orleans Saints safety Steve Gleason blocking a punt by former Atlanta Falcons punter Michael Koenen on September 25, 2006. (Derick E. Hingle via Getty Images)

articles.title: Schottenheimer Says 'Rio Doesn't Define' Cowboys After Taking Blame for Loss Before Win vs. Texans
articles.summary: After a disappointing loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL Rio Game, the Dallas Cowboys managed to bounce back with a dramatic 34-30 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday.
articles.body:
After a disappointing loss to the Baltimore Ravens in the NFL Rio Game, the Dallas Cowboys managed to bounce back with a dramatic 34-30 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who shouldered the blame for the team's Week 3 loss, told reporters after the game that he was motivated to get his team back on track in the midst of a tough stretch.

"Rio doesn't define us as a football team, as a coaching staff here," Schottenheimer said, per ESPN's Todd Archer . "I think I was very upfront and honest with that, but I wanted this game. Why? Because these guys came back off a 10-hour trip. The Ravens, I think, played at home today. We played on the road. We play Thursday night [against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers]. We'll play anybody anywhere and we're looking forward to that, but Rio had nothing to do with this game. This game stood by itself."

New NFL contenders starting to emerge after Week 4

The Cowboys escaped with a win over their in-state rivals thanks to a 12-yard touchdown pass from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb with 40 seconds left in the fourth quarter. Schottenheimer previously said he "didn't do very good in the last 28 seconds" of the loss to the Ravens, so Sunday's win surely boosted morale in Dallas.

"The way I look at this thing, man, is we're hypocrites as coaches if when we make mistakes we don't own up to it," Schottenheimer told Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer . "Obviously, players take a lot of criticism. They take a lot of coaching. And this is a situation where, look, we didn't handle it very well. And if I'm not able to lead from the front and be accountable, then how can I stand up in front of them and ask them to be accountable? It wasn't a fun week, in terms of going through the stuff that comes with it. But I know my players love me."

Schottenheimer will try to build off the momentum of Sunday's win when the Cowboys (2-2) quickly return to action on Thursday Night Football against the Buccaneers (0-4).

articles.title: Steelers Sign New CB After Joey Porter Jr. Trade to Cowboys & Loss to Browns, NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: After trading cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys and losing to the Cleveland Browns last week, the Pittsburgh Steelers reportedly added some depth to their defensive backfield on Monday.
articles.body:
After trading cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys and losing to the Cleveland Browns last week, the Pittsburgh Steelers reportedly added some depth to their defensive backfield on Monday.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , the Steelers are signing veteran CB Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad.

Steelers Refused Guarantee for Porter Jr.

Murphy-Bunting last played during the 2024 season, appearing in 15 games for the Arizona Cardinals. He was placed on the reserve/non-football injury list in May 2025, ruling him out for the entire year. The Cardinals waived him in August, and he signed with the Bucs to return to the franchise with which he spent the first four years of his career.

The Steelers struggled to stop Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson as he led his team down the field to set up a game-winning field goal in the fourth quarter of Thursday night's game. Pittsburgh fell to 2-2 as Cleveland took sole possession of first place in the AFC North at 3-1.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported that the Steelers chose to trade Porter because of their "general philosophy of avoiding second-year guarantees." Porter is in the final year of his rookie deal, and the Cowboys are expected to wait until after the season to address his new contract.

After giving up Porter, the Steelers are hoping that Murphy-Bunting can serve as a reliable replacement as they try to keep pace in the competitive AFC North. Pittsburgh will be back in action in Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts (2-2).

articles.title: B/R Experts Week 5 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: We're one month into the 2026 NFL season, and for everything we think we know, as it turns out there are two we did not.
articles.body:
We're one month into the 2026 NFL season, and for everything we think we know, as it turns out there are two we did not.

We knew that the San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills would be good, and outside Buffalo's Week 4 setback at home both teams have been. But four weeks in not many would have predicted that the New York Giants and Cleveland Browns would be in first place.

Conversely, we figured that the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans would be bad, and sure enough both teams are winless. However, no one figured that the Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers would join those bottom-feeders after both teams made the playoffs a year ago.

After another wild week of NFL action, the league's pecking order has once again gotten the snowglobe treatment. And as is the case every week, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have come together to sift through the week's happenings and rank all 32 teams from worst to first.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Well, the Miami Dolphins didn't lose by double-digits in Minnesota. So there's that.

In fairness, the Miami defense did what it could to keep the team in the game in Week 4. But the Dolphins offense is—offensive. It didn't help that the team's best offensive weapon (running back De'Von Achane) tore his ACL last week. But even with Achane, Miami couldn't move the football.

Now? The Dolphins had all of 198 total yards—and backup running back Ollie Gordon accounted for over half of them. Gordon had as many yards on the ground as quarterback Malik Willis had passing and rushing combined.

It's not improving anytime soon. This is a legitimately terrible football team. It's awfully hard to pick out potential wins on the upcoming schedule. And two shots at the New York Jets (including in Week 7) may be the only thing that stops these Dolphins from taking a run at 0-17. – Davenport

At some point, the Tennessee Titans must get beyond moral victories and finally find ways to win. Sunday's outcome may have only been by one score, but the meeting between the Baltimore Ravens wasn't particularly close.

Baltimore tried to milk a 17-point halftime lead, because quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a high-ankle sprain and didn't play during the second half. Tyler Huntley entered the game and struggled to move the Ravens' offense. Tennessee finally closed the gap in the fourth quarter, but the damage was already done.

Eventually, the Titans will need to see more from last year's No. 1 overall pick, Cam Ward. First-round wide receiver Carnell Tate finally produced a big game, but he also had a drop and fumbled twice. These two are supposed to be Tennessee's primary building blocks. They're not playing like it. -- Sobleski

Even in the NFL's worst division, The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are cooked.

After falling at home to a mediocre Green Bay Packers team, the Buccaneers are winless this season. Dating back to last season's second-half collapse, Tampa has won just twice in their last 13 games.

It's not getting better anytime soon, either. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (He of the recently inked three-year, $165 million extension) is expected to be out at least a couple more weeks with a broken thumb. The NFL debut of undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels went—well it went about like you'd expect. The Buccaneers are not good—on either side of the ball.

The Buccaneers are stuck with Mayfield now. But after the way this team has collapsed dating back to 2025, head coach Todd Bowles is likely living on borrowed time. -- Davenport

In a postgame press conference, Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job isn't in jeopardy, but he should reconsider. The Chargers racked up garbage-time points in their Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, but the team still hasn't figured it out on offense.

Offensively, the Chargers must make significant changes as their season goes further off the rails. They're easily one of the NFL's five worst teams, which is astounding with quarterback Justin Herbert, wideout Ladd McConkey (when healthy), left tackle Rashawn Slater, right tackle Joe Alt and running back Omarion Hampton on the offensive side of the ball. -- Moton

The Houston Texans understand what it means to start poorly then rally to earn a postseason appearance. However, the team has never started 0-4 and made the playoffs. Only one team in NFL history has.

What makes Houston's situation so infuriating is the team could rely on its defense last season. This year is a different story. Houston went from fielding the league's best defense to sitting outside of the Top 20. Houston currently ranks among the bottom five pass defenses.

Derek Stingley Jr. and the Texans' secondary couldn't slow CeeDee Lamb. Instead, Lamb set a new Dallas Cowboys franchise record Sunday with 17 receptions in a single game.

Ironically, Houston's offense was the bigger concern entering the 2026 campaign. It's currently ranked sixth overall. -- Sobleski

Week 4 Result: Lost at New York Giants 36-24

The Arizona Cardinals are who we thought they were. A surprising Week 1 victory has quickly faded and given way to the team everyone expected. Arizona has now lost three straight. Clearly, the team is searching for some kind of answer.

At some point, a change at quarterback will be necessary. The same is true today as it was last season. Jacoby Brissett is a fine backup option. He can lead an offense and put up numbers. But Arizona is now 2-14 with him as its QB1.

Unless a drastic turnaround happens at some point over the next few weeks, rookie Carson Beck should be handed the offense to see what he can do before the team's attention turns toward next offseason. -- Sobleski

The New York Jets had just one victory for the season entering their Week 4 trip to Chicago. But the team had looked improved. Competent. Competitive.

Sunday, they looked like the New York Jets. And that's not good.

Offensively, the Jets couldn't do anything. With Breece Hall sidelined, the run game was all but non-existent, gaining less than 60 yards. Jets quarterback Geno Smith wasn't any better—Smith threw for just 119 yards.

Meanwhile, the Bears had more yards on the ground (232) than the Jets had total yards (157). New York's defense was gouged just as badly through the air—all told the Bears piled up 492 yards of offense and a whopping 34 first downs—with a backup quarterback.

Next week's home date with the Cleveland Browns suddenly feels like the only thing standing between the Jets and another miserable season.

And the end of Aaron Glenn's tenure as head coach. -- Davenport

Week 4 Result: Lost vs. Indianapolis 30-13

The Washington Commanders are in real danger of having their season slip away because of injuries for the second straight season. They managed to beat the defending champion Seattle Seahawks with Marcus Mariota at quarterback in Week 3, but they lost Mariota to a knee injury in London on Sunday.

Rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis had a few bright moments against the Indianapolis Colts, but he made his fair share of rookie mistakes, too. Washington's defense showed some signs of progress against Indy, too, but it couldn't stop the ground game late, and the Commanders now sit at 1-3.

Next week's matchup with the rival New York Giants has become a veritable must-win. -- Knox

Will the real Atlanta Falcons please stand up?

Had you said after the team's Week 2 debacle against the Carolina Panthers that Atlanta would be in position to move into first place with a win on Monday night, you'd have been laughed at. The Falcons looked awful.

But that was without Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback. Penix made his first start of the season last week in Green Bay, and the Falcons destroyed the Packers, rushing for 242 yards and amassing almost 500 yards of offense.

If the Falcons can come close to backing up that effort Monday night in New Orleans, then not only did we write Atlanta off too soon…

They may well be the class of the NFC South. – Davenport

The Indianapolis Colts have won two in a row, but they're still not on track.Shane Steichen's squad isn't close to where it was before last season's second-half collapse. Quarterback Daniel Jones was a huge part of that early success. He's been part of the problem to start this season despite the two-game winning streak.

Jones already committed seven turnovers, including five during the last two weeks. Comparatively, the quarterback didn't commit his seventh turnover until Week 9 of the 2025 campaign.

However, the Colts' defense has improved after a horrendous start. DeForest Buckner has been particularly devastating while working along the defensive interior. Plus, Indianapolis always has the luxury of leaning on Jonathan Taylor when the passing game isn't clicking.

As long as Jones does a better job with his ball security, the Colts could easily win their next two contests against the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans. -- Sobleski

With an imbalanced offense, the Green Bay Packers barely beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who started undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels in Week 4. The Packers defense logged two interceptions and forced a turnover on downs to seal the victory.

However, after the game, head coach Matt LaFleur warned his running backs about their poor ball security. As a team, the Packers rushed for a season-high 86 yards, but they desperately need a reliable ground attack to take some pressure off quarterback Jordan Love. Green Bay doesn't have a sustainable winning approach. – Moton

A quick glance at the Saints record might not appear to indicate an improved team. But the Saints two losses have come by nine points combined against quality opponents—and in between those setbacks was a victory over the Ravens in Baltimore.

In his second season, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough looks the part of a franchise quarterback, entering Week 4 at or near the top of numerous statistical categories. Edge-rusher Chase Young is playing like a guy who was once drafted second overall.

The Saints have issues, though. Young may be playing well, but the defense as a whole has been lacking—27th in points per game allowed. With running back Travis Etienne on injured reserve, an already shaky ground game has all but evaporated.

Potential meets flaws. A difficult team to get a bead on.

The Pittsburgh Steelers actually played quite well in the Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals, and it came alive in the second half against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday. However, it's been a struggle to find big plays all season, and Pittsburgh should probably be in the market for a receiver ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

Even more concerning than Pittsburgh's lack of explosives is the play of its defense, which is the most expensive defense in the entire league. The unit has been above average, but it hasn't been able to carry the team while the Steelers' offense finds its rhythm.

Pittsburgh will have a chance to rebound at home against the Indianapolis Colts next week, and it'll be interesting to see how the team responds after tempers flared during the Week 4 loss. -- Knox

John Harbaugh just might keep the New York Giants in the playoff conversation despite losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury.

New York barely scraped by in Jameis Winston's first game as a starter, but it looked much more formidable in Week 4—though Winston's disinterest in ball security was again an issue. The Giants battled back from a 14-3 first-quarter deficit and sealed the win with Deonte Banks' 98-yard walk-off pick-six.

Don't look now, but the Giants are all alone in first place in the NFC East heading into next week's matchup with the Washington Commanders. -- Knox

The Detroit Lions' defensive issues go beyond their missing starting safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph. The Lions had no answer for Tetairoa McMillan, who caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns or Chuba Hubbard, who ran for 122 yards and two scores.

Head coach Dan Campbell needs to re-evaluate the team's defensive structure and game plan with coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. At some point, even with professional backups, the unit must adjust when the opposing team's best pass-catcher and lead ball-carrier go up and down the field with little resistance.

The Lions have a top-five offense and arguably the league's worst defense, which is a recipe for mediocrity. -- Moton

Week 4 Result: Lost vs. Jacksonville 22-17

The Cincinnati Bengals have dropped two in a row, and the injuries of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins suddenly loom very large. Cincinnati's new-look defense has been markedly better than last year's unit, but the Bengals still haven't been good enough to beat quality teams when Joe Burrow isn't at his best.

Cincinnati's two wins have come against teams with a combined 0-8 record.

This still feels like a team that can be a tough out if it reaches the postseason, but that doesn't mean it will be a playoff team. Fortunately, the Bengals will face another winless team when they visit the Miami Dolphins next week. -- Knox

It certainly feels like it's going to be another rollercoaster season for the Dallas Cowboys. Their retooled defense hasn't looked much different from last year's unit, but the Cowboys offense again looks like an elite unit. A week after bad defense and poor clock management led to a last-second loss, Dallas mounted its own late fourth-quarter comeback.

The good news is that blowing it against the Ravens in Brazil didn't break the Cowboys. The better news is that there's still time for Dallas' defense to grow into at least an average unit, which may be all the Cowboys need to make a run at the postseason.

The defense should get a chance to gain some confidence next week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and their undrafted rookie quarterback. -- Knox

Much like the division they play in, the Carolina Panthers aren't an easy team to get a bead on four weeks into the season.

Offensively, the Panthers sometimes look like one of the league's most dangerous offenses. Sunday night's win over the Lions was the third time in four games that Carolina has scored over 30 points. Quarterback Bryce Young isn't just playing the best football of his career—he's playing like a top-10 signal-caller.

Defensively, however, the Panthers have been erratic. This is the team that surrendered 59 points to the Chicago Bears at home back in Week 1. The Lions actually out-gained the Panthers in a shootout that included almost 900 yards of offense.

That defense is going to be a problem if the Panthers get back to the postseason, but in a division filled with flawed teams, Carolina is the front-runner right now. – Davenport

If the New England Patriots shake off their early struggles and make another deep playoff run, we may well look back at this game as the springboard to that success.

Headed into Sunday's meeting with the rival Bills, the New England offense was a mess—three games into the season, the Patriots were averaging a league-low 12 points per game. Last week in Jacksonville, they managed just six.

But it was a different story at Highmark Stadium. Quarterback Drake Maye finally looked like last year's MVP runner-up. The Patriots gashed the Bills for 143 rushing yards. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs found the end zone twice.

A shaky Buffalo defense played a part, but the Patriots got a win they badly needed. And with two straight home tilts up next, New England has opportunity to shake off that early funk and build some real momentum -- Davenport

The Philadelphia Eagles have won two straight NFC East titles, but injuries have them in danger of falling behind in this year's race.

The Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith ahead of Week 4, then watched Saquon Barkley, Quinyon Mitchell, and Jonathan Greenard all exit with injuries. They came close to upsetting the visiting Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, but we're still talking about a banged-up 2-2 squad that recorded its two wins by a combined six points.

Philly needs to get healthy in a hurry because the surging Jacksonville Jaguars are next on the schedule. -- Knox

The Cleveland Browns are sitting at 3-1 a month into the 2026 season, and yet, it's still a little difficult to take this team seriously.

The Browns have won three straight but have won by a combined 10 points. Their defense has been more good than great; they're still trying to get the ground game going, and they overcame a sloppy second half by Deshaun Watson on Thursday night.

That said, Cleveland is significantly better than pretty much anyone expected coming into the season. It has a legitimate chance to move to 4-1 against the New York Jets next week. -- Knox

Week 4 Result: Lost at San Francisco 24-14

So far this season, the Denver Broncos haven't led in any contest going into the fourth quarter. In Week 4, they didn't have enough late-game magic to come back from a deficit.

Aside from a 30-point second-half flurry against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3, the Broncos offense has struggled mightily, and it's still trying to find its groove under new offensive play-caller Davis Webb. Unless head coach Sean Payton reclaims play-calling duties, it could be a bumpy ride for quarterback Bo Nix and his playmakers.

Denver is slowly falling in our power rankings for good reason. -- Moton

Week 4 Result: Lost vs. Kansas City 30-27

For the first time this season, the Las Vegas Raiders came up short, losing to the Kansas City Chiefs, but they're not frauds after entering last week at No. 11 in our power rankings.

In the third quarter, on 4th-and-2, Las Vegas passed up a 41-yard field-goal attempt and turned the ball over on downs. In the final quarter, kick returner Dareke Young fumbled, which allowed league-leading rusher Kenneth Walker III to score on a short field.

While aggressive, the Raiders will miss the mark at times, but they're good enough to hang with the NFL's upper-echelon teams. Keep in mind that playoff-caliber clubs have a better chance of capitalizing on Las Vegas' mistakes. -- Moton

Week 4 Result: Won vs. New York Jets 23-12

Regardless of who takes snaps under center, the Chicago Bears offense remains steady with head coach Ben Johnson calling the plays.

Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent went 25-of-34 passing for 268 yards in a win over the New York Jets. Meanwhile, Kyle Monangai ran for 146 yards and two touchdowns. Chicago can beat opponents in multiple ways, a hallmark of a playoff-caliber squad.

Even without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, the Bears are a top-10 team. -- Moton

Week 4 Result: Won at Philadelphia 24-20

It's fair to say this season has gone according to plan for the Los Angeles Rams. They're not steamrolling opponents. Instead, Sean McVay's squad sits at .500 thanks to inconsistent performances across the board.

Myles Garrett's absence due to injury doesn't help. Star wide receiver Puka Nacua already missed time this season. Cornerback Jaylen Watson is dealing with a dislocated shoulder. Plus, the league's reigning MVP, Matthew Stafford, isn't playing like one. His six interceptions are tied for the league's second-most.

Eventually, the Rams will get all of their top players back. Stafford is experienced enough to cut down on the mistakes. If/when those things happen, Los Angeles could easily look like the league's Super Bowl favorite. The team simply isn't close to that point through four weeks of play. -- Sobleski

Week 4 brought a bit of a mixed bag for the Baltimore Ravens. Their win over the lowly Tennessee Titans only appeared close because of 11 unanswered garbage-time points by Tennessee. However, Baltimore also watched star quarterback Lamar Jackson exit with an ankle injury.

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Jackson is considered day-to-day with the injury.

The Ravens are 3-1 and remain atop the AFC North. However, they're not running away with the division, and they're going to need Jackson close to 100 percent to navigate a difficult upcoming stretch that includes games against the Cincinnati Bengals, Buffalo Bills, and Jacksonville Jaguars in late October and early November. -- Knox

The Minnesota Vikings had the least impressive Week 4 win, eking one out over the winless Miami Dolphins, who lost their best offensive playmaker, running back De'Von Achane, for the season.

Justin Jefferson didn't play last week, but even with him on the field, Kyler Murray has struggled in head coach Kevin O'Connell's system. He's thrown just one touchdown pass since he returned from a concussion in Week 3.

It's hard to hit the panic alarm on anything for a 4-0 team, but the Vikings need more of their starting quarterback if they want to be taken seriously. Carson Wentz may be the better option. -- Moton

Most of the attention placed on the Jacksonville Jaguars tends to involve the offensive side of the ball, whether the discussion centers on quarterback Trevor Lawrence, the continued growth of wide receiver Parker Washington, tight end Brenton Strange, etc. Although, Jacksonville's defense deserves far more attention this season.

Jacksonville has allowed the NFL's second-fewest points (53) through four games. The effort is also the franchise's best since the start of the 2007 campaign. The Jaguars are particularly good at the point of attack. They're ranked second in rushing defense after the Cincinnati Bengals managed a measly 23 yards during Sunday's action.

Liam Coen's squad is clearly the best the AFC South has to offer. -- Sobleski

Week 4 Result: Lost vs. New England 29-26

Entering Week 4, the Bills and Patriots were two teams barreling in opposite directions. The Bills were playing as well as any team in the NFL. The Pats were floundering on offense and has just gotten blown out by the Jaguars.

That floundering offense got right against the Bills—Drake Maye had by far his best game of the season, and New England topped 140 yards on the ground.

It was another rough day for the Bills defensively—and potentially cause for legitimate concern. The Patriots came into the game with the worst scoring offense in the league, but they didn't look it against the NFL's eighth-worst defense.

The Bills aren't the only contender with defensive issues (looking at you, Detroit). But Sunday's home loss exposed just how glaring those issues are – Davenport

Week 4 Result: Won vs. Los Angeles Chargers 30-23

Sam Darnold's return to the lineup has been a bit of a bumpy road. The Super Bowl-winning quarterback threw three interceptions over the last two games. The primary difference between Seattle's loss in Week 3 and a victory in Week 4 was the team's ability to put away the Los Angeles Chargers.

Despite allowing the Chargers to close the gap after building a 21-point second-half lead, the Seahawks didn't let off the gas, particularly on defense. Seattle sacked quarterback Justin Herbert four times and hit him on 10 different occasions.

Plus, the Seahawks were able to overcome 150 penalty yards. Mike Macdonald's squad is talented, but it needs to be more disciplined when the San Francisco 49ers, Denver Broncos, Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears are its next four opponents. -- Sobleski

In a battle for first place in the AFC West, the Kansas City Chiefs flexed their muscle as the division's team to beat. Kenneth Walker III ran for a career-high 177 yards and two touchdowns. He's clearly the team's offensive engine, though Patrick Mahomes has done his part with nine touchdown passes and only two interceptions.

According to The Athletic's Mike Silver , the Chiefs have reached out to Tyreek Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus.

If Hill is healthy enough to play by late October or early November, the Chiefs offense could take off after Thanksgiving. Kansas City is a top team that may get better in a few weeks. -- Moton

The San Francisco 49ers are doing what they normally do, which makes them the NFL's best team.

Once again, the Niners' lineup is littered with injuries. Even so, Kyle Shanahan's squad remains undefeated, with the league's best point differential. Brock Purdy is playing better than any other quarterback. His offensive line isn't allowing pressure. Wide receiver Mike Evans and tight end George Kittle are still weapons. Plus, San Francisco features a top-three scoring defense.

To Shanahan's credit, the 49ers are always among the league's best coached teams. This group is always prepared to play despite whatever extenuating circumstances it faces. As long as the injury issues don't reach the team's star performers, as they did last season, San Francisco can make some serious noise. -- Sobleski

articles.title: Bears' Ben Johnson Names QB1 for Packers Rivalry Game Amid Caleb Williams Injury
articles.summary: Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson wasted little time in naming Tyson Bagent the team's starting quarterback for its Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson wasted little time in naming Tyson Bagent the team's starting quarterback for its Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers.

Bagent went 25-of-34 for 268 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception in a 23-12 win over the New York Jets in Week 4. That came after veteran Case Keenum went 24-of-34 for 247 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions in a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3 after Bagent was in concussion protocol.

Williams has been sidelined since he was carted off the field during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Sept. 27 the setback was a Grade 2 hamstring injury that doctors estimated would sideline the quarterback for three to four weeks. They also noted "Williams likely felt scar tissue breaking up from a past hamstring injury, a phenomenon that can be quite painful to experience but doesn't lead to long-term damage."

While it wasn't the season-ending setback the Bears surely feared as their franchise quarterback was being carted off the field with a towel draped over his head, it was still a significant setback for a team that entered the season with realistic playoff expectations as the reigning NFC North champions.

Williams threw for 3,942 yards, 27 touchdowns and seven interceptions during the 2025 campaign and seemed to pick up where he left off with four total touchdowns in the season-opening win over the Carolina Panthers.

However, he struggled in rainy conditions against the Vikings even before the injury.

With Keenum and Bagent, though, Chicago has won each of its past two games to improve to 3-1 on the season. Now, it will be up to Bagent to try to extend the winning streak to three games as the Bears try to keep pace with the Vikings in the NFC North.

articles.title: Week 5 NFL betting, odds: Bears are favorites against Packers at Lambeau Field for first time in 20 years
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are short road favorites at Lambeau Field -- something that hasn't happened since the Bears went to the Super Bowl in 2006.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears moved to 3-1 on the season with a dominant 23-12 win at Soldier Field over the New York Jets on Sunday. The Bears had a remarkable 34 first downs (to the Jets' seven) and 492 yards of total offense to New York's 157.

The Green Bay Packers improved to 2-2 on the season with a far less impressive 17-14 road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and rookie QB Jalon Daniels. Respected money came in on Tampa Bay to push the line down to Packers -2.5, so Green Bay ended up covering the closing line. That was the Packers' first win against the spread this season.

Chicago heads to Green Bay in Week 5 and the Bears were 2.5-point favorites at sportsbooks on Monday morning. Why is this notable?

Because if the line holds, it would be the first time that the Bears have been favored at Lambeau Field in over 20 years.

Yes, the last time that Chicago walked into Green Bay as a favorite was back on Sept. 10, 2006 — Week 1 of that season — when the Bears closed as 3.5-point favorites. Chicago won that game 26-0 thanks to 262 passing yards from Rex Grossman, two Brett Favre interceptions and a Packers lost fumble. That season ended for the Bears in the Super Bowl — a 29-17 loss to Peyton Manning and the Indianapolis Colts.

The Bears are 3-1 against the spread this season, and have won games straight-up and ATS with Caleb Williams, Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent starting.

Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury against the Minnesota Vikings in a Week 2 loss, and was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Jets. Head coach Ben Johnson confirmed on Monday that Bagent will start again on Sunday against Green Bay.

The Packers were a three-point home favorite this offseason in the lookahead lines at DraftKings Sportsbook.

articles.title: Fred Warner Calls Out Doubters After 49ers Beat Broncos to Stay Undefeated in NFL Standings
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers appear to be a team on a mission this year after remaining undefeated with Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers appear to be a team on a mission this year after remaining undefeated with Sunday's 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos.

49ers star linebacker Fred Warner told Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated after the victory that the team is playing with a chip on its shoulder after being doubted heading into the 2026 campaign.

"I think that people didn't—I don't know—I guess they didn't really take us very seriously before the season started because we did have a lot of guys who were quote-unquote older, and guys who were coming off of injuries," Warner said. "So I think the thing that separated us all along was, yeah, we have a lot of talent, but we have guys that regardless of whatever we've achieved in this league, we're all hungry to continue to get better. And continue to prove it every single week."

The 49ers overcame a slew of injuries last season to finish 12-5 and earn a spot in the playoffs, though they lost to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 41-6 in the Divisional Round.

Warner admitted that the past disappointments have fueled San Francisco amid its scorching start.

"You definitely are aware of that, and I've been super grateful and blessed to be a part of this organization and have opportunities to win the whole thing," Warner said. "Obviously, we dealt with some heavy losses, being in [the Super Bowl] twice and not being able to hoist that trophy. So you do realize that you don't have forever with the same group of guys, and you want to make the most of the opportunity."

The 49ers will look to improve to 5-0 when they face the Seahawks (3-1) in a revenge game in Week 5.

articles.title: NFL Legend Lawrence Taylor Says 'Pump the Brakes' on Giants' Success After Win vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: The New York Giants moved to 3-1 on the season after defeating the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday, leaving them alone atop the NFC East standings.
articles.body:
The New York Giants moved to 3-1 on the season after defeating the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday, leaving them alone atop the NFC East standings.

But the team's fast start isn't enough for franchise legend Lawrence Taylor to assume big things are the horizon. At least not yet.

"Let's pump the brakes a bit on that," he told The Athletic's Ian O'Connor on Sunday night. "... They won today. Let's see if this propels them to more winning."

Giants' fans can perhaps be forgiven for feeling the hype. After all, the franchise only has three winning seasons, two playoff appearances and one playoff win since the start of the 2012 season. The team has lost 10 or more games in eight of the past nine seasons heading into 2026. It's been bleak.

But with John Harbaugh now leading a young and ascendant roster, there is hope.

"It's obvious they have good coaching now, and that's how you develop good players," Taylor told O'Connor. "Nothing against (Harbaugh's) predecessors, but he's a proven winner and he knows how to deal with talent. And there's not much more to say about that."

articles.title: Matthew Stafford Called Best QB, 'As Good Mahomes or Better,' by NFL Exec After Rams Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: After leading the Los Angeles Rams to a comeback win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford still has the respect of the rest of the league.
articles.body:
After leading the Los Angeles Rams to a comeback win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford still has the respect of the rest of the league.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to an executive from another team who declared that Stafford is still outperforming the rest of the NFL.

"Still feel good about them," the exec said. "They have the best player in the league at quarterback — when (Matthew) Stafford is on, he's as good as (Patrick) Mahomes or better. They haven't had a game with the two defenders (Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett) full speed yet. And their defense still looks pretty good."

A week after blowing a 16-point lead in a loss to the Denver Broncos, Stafford helped the Rams overcome a 10-point second-half deficit by leading two touchdown drives in the fourth quarter. The 38-year-old completed 32 of his 51 passes for 317 yards in the victory.

At 2-2, the Rams have not looked like the juggernaut many expected them to be, but they still have enough talent to remain among the top contenders in the NFC.

Stafford and the Rams will face another tough test when they host the Buffalo Bills (3-1) on Monday Night Football in Week 6.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Compares Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza QB Room to Alex Smith, Chiefs Situation
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes believes the Las Vegas Raiders choosing to bring top overall pick Fernando Mendoza along slowly behind veteran Kirk Cousins could be comparable to his own journey starting as Alex Smith's backup in Kansas City.
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes believes the Las Vegas Raiders choosing to bring top overall pick Fernando Mendoza along slowly behind veteran Kirk Cousins could be comparable to his own journey starting as Alex Smith's backup in Kansas City.

"It's going to do a lot of great things for him," Mahomes told reporters Monday regarding Mendoza. "Kirk is a true pro. A quarterback who knows how to run the room, the team, everything the right way. He's gonna do it the right way. ... It'll be great for Fernando to learn and just take in, because you don't know until you're in the NFL. Hopefully not too [great], because it went really well for me and Alex, hopefully maybe not that [great] unless I'm gone or something like that."

Mahomes spent his rookie season as Smith's backup before taking over the starting gig. That's worked out pretty well for the Chiefs.

Mendoza, meanwhile, is the long-term future of the Raiders. But in the short term Cousins has the Raiders looking good. Despite Sunday's 30-27 loss against the Chiefs, Las Vegas has opened the season 3-1 behind Cousins' 1,026 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and four interceptions.

For an organization that has had just two winning seasons since the start of the 2003 campaign, it's been a breath of fresh air. And the hope is that Couins and new head coach Klint Kubiak help turn around the team's culture for the better before the reins are handed over to Mendoza. So far, so good.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' Wife Brittany Trolls Raiders' Klint Kubiak in Photo After Viral Prediction on Video
articles.summary: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes had the last laugh after Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak incorrectly predicted his team would hold onto a halftime lead Sunday.
articles.body:
The wife of Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes had the last laugh after Las Vegas Raiders coach Klint Kubiak incorrectly predicted his team would hold onto a halftime lead Sunday.

Brittany Mahomes posted a series of photos on Instagram from Allegiant Stadium. She included the caption, "We're winning. We're gonna win the game."

That's also what Kubiak told CBS Sports' Tracy Wolfson as he headed for the locker room at the end of the second quarter:

The Raiders maintained a three-point advantage through the third quarter before they collapsed. The Chiefs scored 20 points in the fourth to walk away with a 30-27 victory.

You'd expect any coach in Kubiak's position to be outwardly confident about his team's chances. What else was he supposed to say?

Those inside the Chiefs locker room presumably didn't catch Kubiak's interview, either, as they were focused on their own business.

Brittany Mahomes was clearly paying attention.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Wants Cowboys' George Pickens Traded to Raiders Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: After the Las Vegas Raiders had their three-game win streak snapped with a 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, NBA star Damian Lillard had some advice for his favorite NFL team.
articles.body:
After the Las Vegas Raiders had their three-game win streak snapped with a 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, NBA star Damian Lillard had some advice for his favorite NFL team.

The Portland Trail Blazers veteran point guard took to social media to declare that the Raiders should pursue Dallas Cowboys star receiver George Pickens ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Pickens is set to become a free agent after this season, so the Cowboys could dangle him at the trade deadline to avoid losing him for nothing. Through four games, the 2025 Pro Bowler has caught 18 passes for 225 yards with no touchdowns.

The Raiders didn't have a receiver reach the 100-yard mark in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs, with tight end Brock Bowers leading the team with 86 yards and a touchdown on six catches. Adding a star receiver like Pickens would certainly create a new dimension for Las Vegas' offense, so perhaps Lillard is on to something.

The Raiders (3-1) will try to bounce back when they face the New England Patriots (2-2) in Week 5.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham sends a message to the woman-hating WNBA players with her hat, cranky Prime & Maggie Sajak!
articles.summary: The First Monday of October brings Sophie Cunningham's bold "WOMAN" hat, Deion Sanders' Colorado meltdown and NFL ref drama to Monday Nightcaps.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. First Monday of October. We've got football tonight. We've got playoff baseball tonight. I went out and piped a couple golf balls at the range over the weekend. Might even play a round this week for the first time since July. It'll be nice not to have to bring a towel to the tee box for every hole. Who has it better than us? Nobody. And that's coming from me! All my teams got battered last week, and I'm still pumped to get a new week going. Red Sox? Embarrassed. Gators? Really embarrassed. Dolphins? Actually, not bad! Only lost by five to the Vikes. It would be nice to actually have a lead at some point this season, but I reckon that'll be this week's goal. For now? We move forward. Let's roll. Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham turns her attention to Missouri football and wears a hat that sends a simple, yet blunt message to the woman-hating WNBA girls. You'll see. What else? I've got more ref drama from yesterday's NFL slate, I'm still on the fence about Virginia Tech's "missed" field goal Friday night, and things are going WELL for Deion Sanders out in Colorado. DEION SANDERS DISMISSES MULTIPLE PLAYERS AFTER LOCKER ROOM INCIDENT FOLLOWING COLORADO'S LOSS TO NORTHWESTERN And by that, I mean he might not make it to Halloween. What a fall from grace. Who could've seen it coming?! OK, grab you something tall and strong — please do NOT make it a hurricane (heads up, Tuscaloosa!) — and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! Sophie Cunningham destroyed my Florida Gators on Saturday Have y'all seen that a tropical storm may be eying the great state of Alabama for Saturday's showdown with Georgia? True story. That's the big SEC game this weekend, and Trump's supposed to be in town. Not sure that's gonna happen if these projections pan out ... I'd love to see a good, old-fashioned SEC game in the pouring down rain on Saturday. I love offense. I love scoring. Trust me, I hammered the OVER in last weekend's 'Bama-Miss. State game and it was the most sweat-free bet of all time. But still, I do miss the days where we'd get a nice 20-17 slugfest. We rarely get those anymore. Keep on eye on this one ahead of Saturday. And that ends our meteorological portion of today's class! You are welcome. Now, let's get the week started with Sophie Cunningham wearing a simple "WOMAN" hat to Saturday's homecoming drubbing in Colombia: SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS MESSAGE AFTER PATHETIC FINGER-POINTING TANTRUM & SOX-YANKS ANNOUNCERS WON'T SHUT UP! Things aren't going well out west What a hat. I can't even imagine the insufferable coach of the Minnesota Lynx stumbling upon those pictures today. She'd probably faint. "No Cis, just ..." on the side, and "WOMAN" in the front ... just the perfect hat for Sophie Cunningham. Even in the offseason, she's three steps ahead of the other side. I have a feeling Sophie's about to take it up a notch over these next few months. Stay tuned. PS: Sophie's Tigers absolutely rolled my Gators on Saturday. Typical letdown game for a Florida team the national media just spent a week drooling over. Reminded me of the Dan Mullen years. Disgusting. OK, let's go from one ugly Saturday performance to another, and check in with the state of Colorado athletics. Hey, Deion Sanders ... what's wrong with the fellas? Harbaugh, Va. Tech & the refs are getting out of control "You know what it is. If I say it, you’re gonna run with it, you know darn well what it is," Sanders exclaimed after he was asked what was wrong with the offense. "Write it yourselves… It’s blatant... I’d respect ya'll a lot more if you said it yourself." Yeah, the wheels are just about all the way off in Boulder. Remember a few years ago when Colorado briefly had the football world in the palm of its hand for about half a season? What a time to be alive. The Buffs stunk last year, and they're 2-3 so far this season. Sanders kicked three players off the team last week. His five-star QB mysteriously didn't play last weekend. The offensive line can't protect anyone, which has been a running theme under Sanders in Boulder. It's a mess ... But not as big a mess as what's going on in LA right now! Let's rapid-fire this Monday class and get ready for a big night of playoff baseball and NFL football. First up? The 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers! Not the loudest endorsement for Mike McDaniel I've ever seen ... Look, I watched McDaniel's offenses for four years in Miami. At times, it was a fairytale. The 2023 Miami Dolphins gave me the most enjoyable season I've ever had as a Dolphins fan, which isn't saying much given the organization has stunk my entire life. When it works, it really works. But when it doesn't? It's unfathomably miserable. That's where the Chargers are today. There's no way the Chargers can Jim Harbaugh, right? ... Right? Next? A couple musings from over the weekend, and they all involve the refs. First? These two moments from yesterday were insane to watch, and probably deserve a deeper look: I watched the Vikings one happen live, and couldn't figure out what was going on. The guy was clearly pushed into him. That's gonna happen in football games when you're literally in the trenches with 10 other 300-pound dudes trying to kill each other. What's he so upset about? The ref snapping at Trey McBride in the Cardinals game was wild. Never seen that before. If a player did that to a ref, he'd probably be suspended. He'd certainly be fined out the wazoo. Let's see if Goodell has the stones to do the right thing here. Finally, I know this happened last Friday, but I need everyone's opinion on the controversial field goal from Friday night in Blacksburg. Was this good, or not? I wrote about that Saturday morning, and received dozens of responses. Everyone is on the fence. I still think he made it. What do y'all see there? Let me know! OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week. Strong start to October. Let's keep this train rolling into a big Monday night. articles.title: NFL Suspends Officials Jeff Seeman, Adrian Hill After Viral Videos with Trey McBride, Eric Wilson
articles.summary: The NFL confirmed on Monday that line judge Jeff Seeman has been suspended for two games after he was seen yelling at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride and referee Adrian Hill has been suspended for one game after his response to Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson inadvertently knocking him over, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
articles.body:
The NFL confirmed on Monday that line judge Jeff Seeman has been suspended for two games after he was seen yelling at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride and referee Adrian Hill has been suspended for one game after his response to Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson inadvertently knocking him over, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

The suspensions came for "unprofessional conduct toward a player" and were handed down by NFL vice president of officiating Ramon George.

NFL investigating 2 referees for separate viral exchanges

New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was also in the news after receiving an unsportsmanlike penalty for cursing at an official, a decision that took him by surprise.

"I told him it was a terrible—I'm not going to say effing—call," Vrabel told reporters . "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive."

Seeman's profanities toward McBride quickly went viral and earned a statement in response from NFLPA executive director J.C. Tretter.

"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," he wrote on Sunday. "Players are consistently held accountable when roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

Wilson, meanwhile, said the situation between Hill and himself was a misunderstanding and wasn't a big deal.

"That was funny, honestly," he told reporters after the game. "I ended up apologizing to him and explained the situation. He was cool about it. He understood what was going on. He just said he didn't want us fighting, me and [Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II]. He said he was just trying to break us up."

"I think Adrian's a really good official and does a really good job," Vikings' head coach Kevin O'Connell added on Monday. "And I think that was just kind of a fast moment that happened and we can put it behind us hopefully."

articles.title: Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton reportedly out 12-16 weeks with dislocated ankle, could potentially return by postseason
articles.summary: Whether Thornton sustained the injury while being tackle or as he stood up to celebrate the catch, his left foot wasn't pointed in a natural direction.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton could potentially return late this season from a dislocated ankle, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday .

Per the report, Thornton will undergo surgery this week and have a 12-16 week timeline to return from the procedure, leaving the door open for a potential return in time for the postseason.

Thornton sustained the gruesome injury late in the fourth quarter of Week 4's 30-27 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"It doesn't look good," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters postgame.

With the Chiefs trailing 19-17, Thornton caught a 55-yard pass from Patrick Mahomes on a post pattern, continuing what had been the most productive game of his career. Thornton was tackled by Raiders safety Treydan Stukes and immediately stood up to celebrate the big play. However, he then crumpled to the turf with his left foot turned in an unnatural direction as he sat on the ground.

Warning: Video of the injury is graphic.

Thornton flew home with the team and will be further evaluated in Kansas City.

NFL Network reported Thornton dislocated his ankle, which was put back in place by doctors. He was reportedly "in good spirits."

Thornton suffered the injury while being tackled, though it wasn't clear in live-action when he stood up. Perhaps adrenaline compelled him to celebrate the big play and reality quickly set in as his left foot touched the grass, but replay showed the ankle being dislocated durign the tackle.

Unable to put weight on his left leg, Thornton was carted off the field and taken to the locker room.

As could be expected, Thornton's teammates were upset after seeing how badly he was hurt and watching him require assistance to leave the game. When play resumed, Kenneth Walker scored on a 2-yard run to give Kansas City a 23-19 lead. A subsequent 2-point conversion attempt failed when Mahomes threw incomplete to Walker.

On the ensuing kickoff, Chiefs linebacker Jeffrey Bassa forced Raiders returner Dareke Young to fumble and the ball was recovered by Jack Cochrane at the Las Vegas 22-yard line. One play later, Walker rushed for his second touchdown in 19 seconds. Harrison Butker followed with the extra point for a 30-19 lead.

Thornton, 26, was developing into a reliable big-play threat for Mahomes and a Chiefs receiver corps thinned out by injuries. Rashee Rice left the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury . Xavier Worthy has also been dealing with a shoulder injury, though he played Sunday, notching four receptions.

Because of the injuries, the Chiefs could explore a potential reunion with free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill, The Athletic's Michael Silver reported Sunday night.

Prior to his injury, Thornton caught five passes for 111 yards and two TDs, including an 8-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter.

"Just praying for him, You never want anyone to get injured and you're hoping it's better than it looked out there," Mahomes said to CBS' Tracy Wolfson after the game. "Praying for him and hopefully he comes back healthy."

Thornton missed final 3 games last season with concussion

This is the second consecutive season in which Thornton had to leave a game due to injury.

Last year in a Week 15 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers, he suffered a concussion on a head-to-head hit by safety Tony Jefferson. Thornton missed the Chiefs' final three games as a result.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Giants Role for Commanders Game Discussed by John Harbaugh After Vikings Trade
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy has the chance to move up the depth chart in his second week with the New York Giants.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy has the chance to move up the depth chart in his second week with the New York Giants.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that the quarterback being the No. 2 behind Jameis Winston against the Washington Commanders is a "possibility" and something that's "on the table."

Moving to the second string would be an upgrade for McCarthy, who was demoted to the third-string quarterback with the Minnesota Vikings after losing the battle for the starting job to Kyler Murray.

The Vikings traded McCarthy for a fifth-round pick last week after Giants starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury.

McCarthy has had a rough start to his career, missing all of his rookie season before throwing for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions across 10 games last year.

The rocky start leaves McCarthy with a mental hurdle to overcome as he continues his development. Harbaugh is just focusing on one game at a time with the young quarterback.

"Not really thinking about that," Harbaugh said. "We're just focusing on preparing for the next game, getting him ready for the Commanders game. That's really what we'll be looking to try to get accomplished."

As for whether Winston could be replaced as the starter at some point this season, he at least bought himself another week under center after a strong performance in a win over the Arizona Cardinals.

Winston, who struggled in his first start last week, threw for 250 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions.

He said after the game that the threat of being benched doesn't faze him.

"I'm just grateful for the opportunity I have now. Right now, I get to smile and say, 'I'm the starting QB for the New York Football Giants,'" Winston told reporters . "Focusing on what I would love is winning games with my team, being the best I could be. I'm heating up and I'm starting to get better and better. Last week, I was questioning if I could even throw. This week, I got people talking about the Jameis Winston Experience again."

Barring an injury, it appears Winston will remain under center for the time being, but the Giants must decide between McCarthy and Jake Haener as his backup for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

articles.title: NFL suspends two referees for ‘unprofessional conduct’ toward players
articles.summary: The NFL on Monday said it has suspended line judge Jeff Seeman for two games, and referee Adrian Hill for one game, after contentious interactions with players in different games during Week 4.
articles.body: Two NFL officials whose behavior toward players drew scrutiny Sunday have been sidelined by the league. The NFL on Monday said it has suspended line judge Jeff Seeman for two games, and referee Adrian Hill for one game, after contentious interactions with players in different games during Week 4. The suspensions were handed down by the NFL’s vice president of officiating, Ramon George, and each was issued because of “an instance of unprofessional conduct toward a player,” the league said. Representatives for the unions representing NFL players and referees did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride was coming off the field during the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game against the New York Giants when a sideline camera showed Seeman appearing to use profanity toward McBride. JC Tretter, the executive director of the NFL Players Association, singled out the play as “unacceptable,” he wrote on X Sunday. “Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard.” During the Vikings’ victory against the Dolphins, Hill was knocked over when a first-quarter play was whistled dead but Miami running back Ollie Gordon continued to block Minnesota’s Eric Wilson into Hill. Hill stood up and yelled at Wilson. After the game, Wilson told reporters that he and Hill had spoken about the exchange. “I ended up apologizing to him and explained the situation,” Wilson said. “He was cool about it. He understood what was going on. He just said he didn’t want us fighting.” Seeman has worked as an NFL official since 2002, while Hill started in 2010.

articles.title: NFL suspends referee Adrian Hill, line judge Jeff Seeman after separate player incidents in Week 4
articles.summary: Adrian Hill has been suspended for one game after he got into it with Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson on Sunday.
articles.body:
The NFL suspended a pair of officials on Monday after they were involved in separate incidents with players during games on Sunday.

Line judge Jeff Seeman was suspended for two games on Monday, the league announced, and referee Adrian Hill was suspended for a single game. The suspensions, which were issued by the NFL's vice president of officiating, were due to instances of "unprofessional conduct toward a player."

Seeman got into what appeared to be a heated exchange with Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride on Sunday during their 36-24 loss to the New York Giants. Seeman had some choice words for McBride on the sidelines, which were not picked up by the CBS microphones. The moment came after officials declined to call a pass interference penalty on the defense on a critical third-down attempt to McBride.

NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter called out Seeman on social media after the game.

"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

Hill was involved in an incident with Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson and Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon during Minnesota's 15-10 win on Sunday. Wilson and Gordon were engaged, and Gordon blocked Wilson into Hill, knocking Hill down to the turf hard.

Wilson reached out to offer Hill a hand up, but Hill jumped right up and started screaming at him despite it being Gordon who blocked Wilson into Hill.

The NFL also launched an investigation into that incident, though no penalty or ejection was called in the moment. The game continued on normally.

Hill will be able to return to the field in Week 6 of the season, while Seeman will be sidelined until Week 7.

While things frequently get heated on the field between players and officials, the league didn't waste much time in determining that both Hill and Seeman took things too far on Sunday.

articles.title: Two NFL officials suspended for unprofessional conduct after incidents with players on Sunday
articles.summary: The NFL on Monday suspended two officials after on-field run-ins with players a day earlier.
articles.body: The NFL on Monday suspended a line judge two games for swearing at Arizona’s Trey McBride. Line judge Jeff Seeman was caught on camera cursing at McBride during the Cardinals’ loss at the New York Giants on Sunday. The incident drew the ire of union leader JC Tretter, a retired offensive lineman who played eight seasons. “This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable,” Tretter, the NFL Players Association’s executive director, said on social media along with a video clip of the incident. “Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard.” The interaction took place with just under five minutes left after officials did not call a pass interference or illegal contact penalty on New York’s Dru Phillips, who made contact with McBride before the ball arrived from Jacoby Brissett on a third-and-2 play. Arizona punted and the Giants went on to win 36-24 after Deonte Banks intercepted Brissett’s pass and ran it back for a pick-6 as time expired. Referee Adrian Hill was also suspended for unprofessional conduct in the Miami-Minnesota game. Hill yelled at Eric Wilson and pointed for him to get away after the Vikings linebacker tried to help him to his feet after a collision knocked him over. “I just think it’s one of those situations in kind of a high-energy moment there,” Minnesota coach Kevin O’Connell said Monday. “I think stuff like that can happen sometimes, but I don’t have any major concerns, and I think Adrian’s a really good official and does a really good job. I think that was just kind of fast moment that happened, and we can put it behind us, hopefully.” The league’s vice president of officiating, Ramon George, issued the suspensions. This isn’t the first time an official has been punished for his interactions with a player on the field. Umpire Roy Ellison was punished twice for his behavior. In 2018, he was fined $9,300 and placed on administrative leave for one game after he was accused of calling Buffalo defensive end Jerry Hughes by a derogatory term. Ellison was also suspended for one game in 2013 for making “a profane and derogatory statement” to Washington left tackle Trent Williams.

articles.title: Will Shipley, Eagles RB Depth Chart After Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby Injury Updates
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are suddenly very thin at the running back position.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are suddenly very thin at the running back position.

With Saquon Barkley dealing with a hamstring injury that could cost him time and Tank Bigsby reportedly heading to injured reserve with a core muscle injury that required surgery, the only healthy running back currently on the active roster is Will Shipley.

The Birds do have veteran running backs Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele on the practice squad , and one—or several—of them could be elevated to the 53-man roster this week depending on Barkley's status.

Shipley, 24, will be the likely starter if Barkley can't go. In his three NFL seasons he's rushed for 182 yards and caught 17 passes for 155 yards, largely operating as a special-teams contributor.

Pierce, 26, is the most accomplished of the potential options after rushing for 939 yards and four touchdowns during his rookie season in 2022. He hasn't matched that level of production in the four seasons since, however, but would give the Eagles more of a bruiser to pair with the shiftier Shipley.

Steele, 23, only registered NFL stats during the 2024 season with the Kansas City Chiefs, rushing for 183 yards while adding seven catches for 26 yards. He became something of a fan favorite in Philly during the preseason.

Finally, the 22-year-old Blue rushed for 129 yards and a touchdown for the Dallas Cowboys last season as a rookie but was cut in late August despite the team's limited depth at the position.

The Eagles could also choose to seek external options—perhaps they could trade one of the four quarterbacks they've been keeping on the roster despite a litany of injuries at other positions—though with several options on the practice squad and the uncertainty on just how long Barkley will be out, promoting an internal option from the practice squad probably makes the most sense.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy Says Aaron Rodgers NSFW Exchange Wasn't 'Normal' After Viral Steelers-Browns Video
articles.summary: One of the most notable moments of Thursday's game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns came when Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy exchanged profanities, which the head coach said "wasn't normal" even though they've worked together for so long.
articles.body:
One of the most notable moments of Thursday's game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns came when Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy exchanged profanities, which the head coach said "wasn't normal" even though they've worked together for so long.

"I wouldn't classify it as normal, no," McCarthy told reporters Monday. "But I think the reality of it is it's a 20-year relationship. I think the fact that we were able to sit and talk numerous times over the weekend about that and a number of things.

"Not to put any pressure on my daughter, I'm getting to the grandfather age. I don't want to be saying those type of words, but it's an emotional competitive environment. I think it's something that we can definitely learn from."

Vid of 49ers LB Confronting Broncos HC 😳

Rodgers appeared frustrated that it was taking so long for a play call to get to the huddle and yelled accordingly, which prompted McCarthy to respond by calling him a "f--king a---hole."

The entire thing was captured on camera during the Prime Video broadcast.

It was a frustrating evening for the Steelers, who lost the game 27-24. While Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns, he was also intercepted twice and sacked five times.

Even when the offense settled in and scored two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, the second of which tied the game in the final two minutes, the Pittsburgh defense failed to prevent the Browns from driving into scoring position for the game-winning field goal by Andre Szmyt.

McCarthy was the head coach for Rodgers with the Green Bay Packers from 2006-18 as well. The pair won a Super Bowl together and made the playoffs nine times. There is a long-standing relationship in place, and Thursday surely wasn't the first time there was tension between them.

Still, McCarthy expressed regret for using the words that he did, especially after it was aired on the national broadcast.

Following his exit from Texas Tech over the offseason, Brendan Sorsby is turning his attention towards the 2027 NFL draft.

The quarterback posted a video of himself working out, saying that he wants to "Leave the past in the past. Learn from it, grow from it."

After admitting to placing thousands of bets totaling more than $90,000 while in college, Sorsby received a temporary injunction against the NCAA that would have allowed him to play the 2026 season.

He instead chose to pursue the NFL via the supplemental draft, but the league opted not to hold one. That meant Sorsby would have to wait until 2027 to be drafted.

Sorsby was one of the top transfers in college football this offseason after throwing for 2,800 yards, 27 touchdowns and five interceptions along with 580 rushing yards and nine scores on the ground with Cincinnati in 2025.

His ideal scenario would have been to prove himself as a top pick with the Red Raiders, but he'll instead have to hope an NFL team is willing to take a chance on him after a year away from the game.

articles.title: Joe Mixon, Seahawks Agree to Contract amid Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet Injuries
articles.summary: The reigning Super Bowl champions are adding veteran help to their running back room with rookie Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet also sidelined.
articles.body:
The reigning Super Bowl champions are adding veteran help to their running back room with rookie Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet also sidelined.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Monday the Seattle Seahawks are signing former Cincinnati Bengals and Houston Texans running back Joe Mixon, who will wear No. 25 with the team. Mixon appeared to confirm the news:

Tyreek makes another cryptic post amid Chiefs rumors

Mixon will join the practice squad, according to head coach Mike Macdonald .

Running back depth has become an area of concern for the Seahawks in the early going this season. Most notably, Price will miss at least four games on IR because of a chest injury.

"This is just what happens in football. Unfortunately, injuries happen," Macdonald told reporters . "He can't control these things. He's done everything we've asked him to do since he got here. He's had a great attitude. He's been a great teammate. He has a great future. He's going to play great football for us when he comes back, whenever that is ... It's just unfortunate."

As for Charbonnet, he is yet to play this season as he recovers from a torn ACL. However, Seattle opened his 21-day practice window on Thursday, suggesting he could be nearing his return.

With both of them out for Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers, Emanuel Wilson thrived in the primary running back role. He finished with 21 carries for 81 yards and one touchdown to go with three catches for 39 yards and another score.

Backup George Holani tallied seven carries for 18 yards.

Given Wilson's success, Mixon surely won't come into Seattle and dominate the opportunities in the running game if he does see action in future games. However, he does provide a veteran presence to the depth chart and someone who can help the position tread water until Price and Charbonnet are ready to return.

Mixon played seven seasons for Cincinnati and surpassed the 1,000-yard mark on the ground four times, including when he was a Pro Bowler in 2021. He was also a Pro Bowler in 2024 with the Texans when he ran for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns.

However, the 30-year-old missed the 2025 campaign because of a foot injury. Houston released him in March, which is why he was available for the Seahawks.

articles.title: Sean McVay addresses Rams coach flipping off Eagles fans: ‘Won’t be an issue moving forward’
articles.summary: Video shows Los Angeles Rams coaches exchanging gestures with Eagles fans, with at least one staff member appearing to give the middle finger.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams pulled off a wild comeback against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, but some members of Sean McVay's coaching staff apparently got a little too caught up in the moment. In response to questions from OutKick on Monday, a Rams spokesperson provided comments from McVay's news conference in which the head coach said he had addressed the incident with his staff. "Yep, we talked about it. We'll be better in those situations," McVay said. Video circulating on social media showed Rams coaches celebrating inside their booth at Lincoln Financial Field while exchanging words and gestures with Eagles fans on the other side of the glass. NFL REFEREES JEFF SEEMAN AND ADRIAN HILL SUSPENDED AFTER UNPROFESSIONAL CLASHES WITH PLAYERS IN WEEK 4 At least one member of the Rams staff appeared to give fans the middle finger during the exchange. The video also showed objects, including what appeared to be drinks, being thrown toward the coaches' booth. The staff member making the gesture appears to be Rams assistant offensive line coach Brian Allen, although the team has not confirmed that identification. Allen is in his first season as an assistant offensive line coach after working with the Rams as a consultant in 2025. A former Rams center, Allen appeared in 50 regular-season games for Los Angeles, including 32 starts. He also started all four playoff games during the team's Super Bowl LVI championship run following the 2021 season. The Rams beat the Eagles, 24-20, despite trailing 20-10 in the fourth quarter. The incident appeared to take place just after Los Angeles running back Kyren Williams scored the go-ahead touchdown with 1:10 remaining. OutKick asked the Rams to identify the coaches involved and whether any disciplinary action had been taken. The team's response did not provide either detail. CHIEFS' TYQUAN THORNTON DIDN'T REALIZE HIS FOOT WAS POINTING THE WRONG DIRECTION AFTER GAME-CHANGING CATCH McVay acknowledged that emotions can run hot for coaches working from the booth, saying he experienced that himself earlier in his career with Washington. "You get excited and emotional," McVay said. "We'll learn from that. We'll be better." "Those fans are really into it, but I know that we want to make sure that we're representing the class and the calm steadiness that we want to have, while also being emotionally into it," McVay said. "We did talk about it and that won't be an issue moving forward." McVay isn't asking for silence in the booth. He's asking his coaches to keep their celebrations from turning into confrontations with fans. And let's be fair: some Eagles fans weren't exactly passive observers here (shocking, we know). articles.title: Chiefs get major timeline for potential Tyreek Hill signing
articles.summary: The buzz for Tyreek Hill to Kansas City is growing after a report on Sunday night. On Monday, Hill's timeline to sign with a team was revealed and it is very...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs enter their bye week at 4-0 and are coming off a huge division win against the Las Vegas Raiders . However, the most notable part of the game was the injuries to the wide receiver room.

First, Rashee Rice went down for the game, which was already a big loss. Then, Tyquan Thornton went down with a significant injury.

"Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated left ankle Sunday that was later put back into place by team doctors, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Thornton exited Allegiant Stadium on crutches after his team's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. In the fourth quarter, he had to be carted off the field after he made a 55-yard catch that ended when he was tackled from behind by rookie free safety Treydan Stukes," ESPN's Nate Taylor wrote.

With the WR room taking a big hit, Taylor also reported that the team has been in discussions with Tyreek Hill about a potential reunion.

"Even before the injuries to Thornton and fellow receiver Rashee Rice on Sunday, the Chiefs had already shown interest in signing wide receiver Tyreek Hill, who is a free agent. Following Sunday's game, a team source said "we've remained in contact" with Hill and his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Taylor wrote.

However, it remains to be seen exactly when that could happen if a signing does take place. Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, revealed that he could sign this week.

"I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days," Rosenhaus said.

If Hill signs this week with a team, it would be crazy to see him back this fast after such a significant injury, even with it being a year later. Specifically, if he signs with the Chiefs, they are on a bye week, giving him more time to be ready for their next game.

In a depleted WR room, one would think that Hill would become the favorite target for Patrick Mahomes considering their history together. While it is unclear if Hill will pick Kansas City, that is where many think he will go, and it could happen very soon.
